verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD 69d001e8 and confirmed by a failing test run on a copy of the tree.

The trace:
1. A recorded session chain makes the box, so it isn't someone else's. `lovejoin.ts:8075` computes `received = (await this.someoneElses(...)).length > 0`. someoneElsesOf (:2671) starts from depositsOf (:2095), which drops recorded boxes (`!known(b)`), so `received` is false.
2. No account is tied. depositAccountOf (:2364) does `if (chain) return chain.session === undefined ? (chain.account ?? 0) : undefined;`. The MixEntry branch (:2367) gives a session's entry undefined the same way. `depositors` holds public accounts only. The `origins` branch needs `told?.public`. So `deposited` is undefined, and `payer` is undefined unless the public account pays.
3. So no origin is written. :8085 `const own = received ? receivedIn(...) : boxFrom(...)` and :8086 `origin = spent || received ? merged([...]) : undefined` leave origin undefined. Then :8171 `...(origin ? { origin } : tiedOrigin(built.txHash, ties))` writes nothing, because tiedOrigin (:2381-2382) ties public accounts only.
4. The history reads it as a box. activity.ts:797-798 `case "lovejoin-withdraw": return boxFrom(entry.txHash);` gives `{id: box:<tx>, origin: "lovejoin"}`. historiesByTx's session merge (:819-831) applies only to session-out and session-back entries (rpc.ts:153 entrySession), so it doesn't rescue this one. G6a's copy rule in classesOf re-classes received rows only.
5. The stealth mint takes it first. build.rs:2484-2490 Purpose::Mint ranks Lovejoin 0, Received 1, Session 4. In apart step 1 (:2830), one_more sorts by (last, rank, lovelace), so the stealth mint (wasm lib.rs:2490) takes it first when it pays alone. So does the pool start (lib.rs:2801, launch.rs:791), whose default is the private balance (LovejoinLaunch.tsx:103).
6. The words claim otherwise.
   - The anyway warning (en.json:998) says only "anyone can tie your deposit to your private balance".
   - mint.privacy.fromPrivate (en.json:1464, changed this round) says "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account".
   - privacy.md:107 says "No payer knows a box back from a mix, so a box that pays alone goes first". The unmixed box isn't back from a mix, and privacy.md:446 itself calls such a box "tied to the session".
   - tests/lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:256-257 pins `origin` undefined for the own deposit's way back.

The siblings:
- Bring every box back now (:7765) and a private Bootstrap's box both go through the same withdrawOne.
- So does the retired pools' run, which needs no press.
- So does a session collateral's box: depositAccountOf matches `c.deposit` only, not `tail.deposit`.
- An unsure box brought back anyway gets box:<tx> too. someoneElsesOf needs an origins answer, so a stranger's planted box read while Koios fails comes back as a box. The test shows it.

On chain the link is public. The new Seedelf ties to the box, then to the session's deposit and its one-time account, then to the funding's private inputs. Where that funding spent money made private, the tie reaches the public account. The stealth mint and its note promise to avoid exactly that.

Who can cause it:
- The user, with a warned Bring it back anyway or Bring every box back now. The wallet's own coin pick then makes the link.
- The retired pools' run, with no press at all.
- The unsure sibling needs a stranger to plant a box, Koios to fail, and an anyway press.

Preconditions are real: a chain stopped after its deposit, the box brought back, then a private-balance stealth mint or pool start that the box's way back pays alone.

Part of this predates the round. Before (b) the box ranked 1, already ahead of Unknown, Own and Session money. (b) moves it ahead of received money, and the round's new mint note makes the claim wider than the code. That's medium: a privacy link made by the wallet's own pick, and a claim wider than the code.

What I checked that holds:
- e1a#1 classes a known stranger's box `received:<tx>` (lovejoin-someone-else passes).
- PRIV-3 still ties a public deposit's way back to its account.
- The WebAssembly package at 17:16 carries (b): copied-register-payment's (b) test passes.
- settleWithdrawing (:8288) re-uses the origin the withdraw kept, so a fix in withdrawOne covers the maybe-sent path too.

Test result on unmodified HEAD code: all 3 new tests fail.
- The recorded session chain: origin written null; class read `{id: box:…, origin: lovejoin}`; Bob's 60 ₳ is `received`; the stealth mint spends only the session's unmixed box's way back.
- The restore case: origin null.
- The unsure sibling: origin null, read as lovejoin.

Prototype check (scratch copy only, now deleted): adding sessionClass to the origin in withdrawOne made tests 1 and 2 pass. Over 62 Lovejoin, class, mint and withdraw test files, 1018 tests passed. The only failure was lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:257, which pins today's behaviour and needs changing as the finding says.
verdicts.fix_notes:
All in extension/src/background/lovejoin.ts unless named.

1. Add `depositSessionOf(s, b)` beside depositAccountOf (:2362). It returns the private session whose deposit made box b, while no mix has moved it, looking in this order:
   - the chain with `c.deposit === b.txHash || c.tail?.deposit === b.txHash`, giving `c.session`;
   - the MixEntry whose `(e.deposit ?? (e.bootstrap || e.seed ? e.id : undefined)) === b.txHash` (copy depositAccountOf's own lookup), giving `e.session`;
   - after a restore, `s.origins[b.txHash]`, only when `mixedFor(told, poolOf(b)) === false`, matching an input `cred` against keys.oneTime.keyHash(i) for the indices oneTimeKeys covers (sessionIndices plus GAP_LIMIT past). Derive that before `this.update`, as `received` is.

   The `mixedFor(...) === false` check is essential. A mix that a session's one-time account paid for also has that key among its non-mix_box inputs, and PRIV-3 keeps a mix's output a plain box. A prototype without the check would tie mixed boxes.

2. In withdrawOne at :8085-8086, when `!received`, merge `sessionClass(i)` in:
   `origin = spent || received || i !== undefined ? merged([own, ...(i !== undefined ? [sessionClass(i)] : []), ...(spent ? [spent.class] : []), ...(ties ?? []).map(madePrivate)]) : undefined`.
   The id becomes `box:<tx>+session:<i>` with origin "session". The ranks follow:
   - Mint takes it last (4).
   - A funding ranks it as another session's money (tier 1), or 0 for that session's own top-up.
   - Pay ranks it 1.
   - The UTxOs screen shows both tags.
   This also covers Bring every box back now, a private Bootstrap, a collateral tail box and the retired pools' run, since all of them go through withdrawOne.

3. When the box is unsure at the update (`!knownOf(s)(box)` and not received), write `unknownIn(built.txHash)` in place of box:<tx>. That covers Bring one back anyway on an unsure box, and Bring every box back now, which asks nobody. A retired pool's box that was never asked lands here too, ranked after received money for Mint, which is the conservative side.

4. Tests:
   - Change lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:256-257: the own deposit's way back expects `{id: "box:<tx>+session:0", origin: "session"}`.
   - Add the three tests below, citing "chunk 51, own#4".

5. Residual to state in the record: history entries already written without an origin keep reading box:<tx>, and (b) now ranks them first. These come from 1.8.0's retired-pool run and earlier anyway presses. The entry doesn't keep the box's outpoint, so they can't be re-classed without a lookup.

6. Docs:
   - privacy.md:168: a box brought back unmixed carries its deposit's session, as :433 says for a public account's deposit.
   - privacy.md:81, :107 and :172, and mint.privacy.fromPrivate, then hold as written, since only box:<tx> goes first. If the fix doesn't land, they are wider than the code.
   - architecture.md: list the class `box:<tx>+session:<n>`.

7. No new record is kept, only the value in the existing history `origin` field, so it likely needs no privacy-policy entry. G8 or the lead should confirm.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds. Every cited line is accurate on HEAD 69d001e8.

**How the box gets classed box:<tx>**
- Recorded chain: lovejoin.ts:2364 `if (chain) return chain.session === undefined ? (chain.account ?? 0) : undefined;` gives undefined for a session's chain.
- After a restore, :2371-2372 ties only an origin with `public`.
- someoneElsesOf (:2671-2674) never names an own box. depositsOf skips recorded boxes, and `ours` (:2673) excludes a deposit paid by one of the phrase's one-time keys. So :8075 `received` is false.
- :8085-8086 then leave `origin` undefined (no spent, no received). :8171 and settleWithdrawing's :8290 write `tiedOrigin(tx, undefined)`, which is `{}`.
- activity.ts:797-798 then classes the entry `boxFrom(tx)`, origin "lovejoin". entrySession (rpc.ts:153) reads only session-out/back entries, so historiesByTx never merges it into the session. activity.ts `classes` reclasses only rows classed received, so this row is untouched.
- tests/lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:256-257 pins this for a deposit paid by one-time key 0.

**What the round changed**
- build.rs:2484-2490: Mint is now Lovejoin 0, Received 1, Unknown 2, Own 3, Session 4. At 984ff48f it was Received 0, Lovejoin 1.
- one_more (build.rs:2725, ranked at :2830) takes the lowest-rank single UTxO that pays, whatever its size. So this box now goes before any received UTxO, for a stealth mint (wasm lib.rs:2490) and for a private pool start (:2801).
- For a wallet with no received money nothing changed: the box already ranked ahead of Own and Session.

**Nothing later catches it**
- CreateSeedelf has no UTxO choice. The review shows only "Paid from".
- historiesNote is silent for a single class (histories.ts:209 `classes.length > 1`).
- The UTxOs screen tags the UTxO "Back from Lovejoin".
- The round's 8bf4aaca widened mint.privacy.fromPrivate (en.json:1464) from "Only money others paid you keeps…" to "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account". That is false for this box when the session was funded with money made private.
- privacy.md:107 says "No payer knows a box back from a mix, so a box that pays alone goes first". The code does not tell a mixed box from an unmixed one.
- The wallet's own words call such a box the session's: lj.tail.privacy.wayOut (en.json:948) says "stays in the pool unmixed, tied to this session". A session's direct return is already classed sessionClass, which Mint ranks last.

**Who can reach it**
The user, never a stranger, for the own-box case. It needs all three:
1. A box still at its own session's deposit: a chain cut by a lock, a closed browser or a refused first mix; a session collateral box left by "Bring the rest back now"; a private Bootstrap box; or a Lovejoin-tile private mix cut at its deposit.
2. A way back for it: a warned "Bring it back anyway" (the warning only says the deposit ties to "your private balance", nothing about later spends), Bring every box back now, or, with no press at all, a retired pool's run.
3. A later stealth mint, which is opt-in (the account is the default payer, CreateSeedelf.tsx:64), or a private pool start, which defaults to private. The box must be the smallest rank-0 UTxO that pays alone.

**What is lost**
No funds. The payer-hiding the user picked the private mint for is gone. Anyone can tie the new Seedelf to the deposit, the session's one-time account and its dApp activity, and the funding's private inputs. Where those were made private, the tie reaches the public account. Before the round, a received UTxO that pays alone would have been taken instead, and only its payer could make that link.

**Also checked**
- ChainRecord.session uses sessionClass's index. The chain record is kept while an unmixed box of it is listed (lovejoin.ts:6234-6235), so the session index is still there at withdraw time.
- depositAccountOf matches only `c.deposit`, never `c.tail.deposit`. A fix that copies its pattern would miss the collateral box.
- An unsure box (no origin yet) also falls to boxFrom, because depositsOf needs `mixedFor(...) === false`.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. **A helper for the session.** In lovejoin.ts beside depositAccountOf, add `depositSessionOf(s, b)`. It returns the session whose own deposit put `b` where it is, with no mix moving it since:
   - A chain with `c.session !== undefined` and either `c.deposit === b.txHash` or `c.tail?.deposit === b.txHash` (the collateral box).
   - Else a MixEntry with `session !== undefined` whose depositOf is b.txHash (a private Bootstrap).
   - Else, after a restore, the index whose one-time key is among `s.origins[b.txHash].inputs`. oneTimeKeys (:6650) returns a Set; give it a variant that returns a Map from key hash to index.

2. **Compute it before the update.** withdrawOne's update callback is synchronous, so compute the session before `this.update`, as `received` is at :8075.

3. **Class the way back at :8085-8086.**
   - `own` = received ? receivedIn(tx) : session !== undefined ? merged([boxFrom(tx), sessionClass(session)]) : boxFrom(tx).
   - Set `origin` when session !== undefined too.
   - Because `origin` goes into s.withdrawing, settleWithdrawing (:8286-8290) writes the same class after a lock.
   - Result: Mint 4, Fund 5 (0 for that session's own top-up), Pay 1, tagged "Private session N".
   - sessionClass alone is simpler, and more honest for the tag, if the "Back from Lovejoin" tag shouldn't show.

4. **The unsure box.** Class a box whose making isn't known at withdraw (`!knownOf(s)(box)`) as unknownIn(tx), which Mint ranks 2. Retired-pool boxes coming back by themselves aren't asked of Koios. Decide whether this rule should cover them, or only Bring one back anyway and Bring every box back now.

5. **Past withdraws.** Entries already written with no origin (for example unmixed session boxes from 1.8.0's retired run) stay box:<tx>. Nothing on the device maps a withdraw to its box, so either accept this or say it in the docs.

6. **Words.**
   - privacy.md:81, :107 and :172, and architecture.md:706 (beside the receivedIn sentence), should say that a box your own session deposited and no mix moved comes back as that session's money, and the stealth mint takes it last.
   - mint.privacy.fromPrivate is right again once the class is fixed. Leave it alone; no new critical strings are needed.
   - No privacy-policy entry: nothing new is sent or kept.

findings.title: spentBy lives only in session storage: if the wallet locks after a non-balance read folds another profile's spend, the spender is lost and that change reads as received
findings.scenario:
1. Profile B spends from the private balance (tx T).
2. Profile A, unlocked, builds a private review. readContract calls readIndexView, which:
   - folds T's change into the sealed rows;
   - moves the sealed cursor past T (:384);
   - adds T to the session view's spentBy (:412).
   No arrived() runs.
3. A locks before the next balance reading (auto-lock, say). The session view is wiped, and spentBy with it.
4. After unlock, since() starts past T, so the reading hands arrived() no spender. T's change is still fresh in `seen` and is noted Received. The stealth mint and fundings then take it ahead of own money: the harm gap-g9#1 fixes.

Also, this cache is the fixer's addition to the decision's "no record". architecture.md:419 names it, but privacy.md's on-device lists and the policy don't.
findings.who: nobody (the user's second profile plus a lock)
findings.evidence:
contract-scan.ts:384 `if (next.cursor !== settled.cursor || unchecked.length) await seal(store, record, next);`
contract-scan.ts:412 `const view: Kept = { ..., ...withSpentBy((await session.get<Kept>(key))?.spentBy, spentBy) };`: session storage, wiped on lock.
balances.ts:304, :435 are arrived()'s only callers.
activity.ts:572 `...(h.first && before(u) ? { origin: UNKNOWN } : elsewhere(u))`
findings.fix:
Pick one:
- Run arrived() whenever readIndexView folds a spend of the wallet's own rows.
- Seal the (spender, refs) pairs with the contract record until arrived() has seen their change.
- Accept the window.

If the cache stays, add a line to privacy.md's On this device.
findings.owner_question: Keep the session cache (then add a privacy.md line), seal the pairs, or drop it as the decision's 'no record' had it?

verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD 69d001e8 (.), every cited line opened. The finding holds; no guard was missed.

1. Where the spender starts. contract-scan.ts:358-365 builds `spentBy` from the answer: for each spend of one of the wallet's own rows, the spender's hash. :384 `if (next.cursor !== settled.cursor || unchecked.length) await seal(store, record, next);` seals the new cursor on every read, a balance reading or not. :412 `const view: Kept = { ..., ...withSpentBy((await session.get<Kept>(key))?.spentBy, spentBy) };` keeps the spenders only in the session view (`seedelf.contract.<net>`). They are not in the sealed `Settled` record (:246-257, :374-383).

2. How long T's spend is visible. The cursor sits on a 200-slot grid, at least 200 slots below the tip (seedelf-data/README.md:122; tests/fake-index.ts:17). So T's spend is in `since` answers only until some read's answer cursor passes T's slot. That read seals the cursor past T, and later answers never name T again.

3. Reads that don't run arrived(). These all call readContractView: script-spend.ts:233 `readContract` (Make public/Withdraw, Transfer, Mint, lovejoin-launch.ts:349, sessions.ts:3164, and lovejoin.ts:8013, which includes the worker's box-back paid from the private balance), send.ts:74, transfer.ts:74 and sessions.ts:5318. None calls arrived(); grep finds only balances.ts:304 and :435.

4. Balance readings are rare within a session. They run only with no cached reading, on Refresh, or when the private side is marked stale (balances.ts:217-236; Home.tsx:322-376). Home's 20 s timer (:452) reads sessions and Lovejoin, not balances. So the read that crosses the cursor is often a review's or the worker's.

5. The lock. wallet.ts:339-347 `lock()` calls `wipe()` (:729-740), which runs `session.clear()` and puts back only SESSION_SENDS and SESSION_DAPP_REFUSED. A closed browser or an update clears session storage too. Nothing else drops the view: accounts.ts:97 leaves it at an account switch, forgetContractView (:447-453) and readKoiosView (:220) keep spentBy, and a refused `keep` (:460-466) also loses it.

6. After the unlock. readIndexView reads `since(<sealed cursor past T>)`, so `spentBy` is `{}`, `withSpentBy(undefined, {})` gives no spentBy, and balances.ts:435 hands arrived() nothing for T.

7. How C gets read. The history is sealed (`history.<net>`, activity.ts:763-777). `seen` lacks C, since no arrived() ran. `first` was dropped by the first arrived() (:591-595). So :572 takes `elsewhere(u)`, where `spentBy[T]` is undefined, which gives `{}`. The entry is kind "received" with no origin, and classOf :795-796 gives `receivedIn(T)`. The stealth mint and fundings then take C first.

8. Docs. privacy.md:177 and flows.md:110 say, without exception, that on mainnet a spend of this device's UTxOs is "Already in your private balance". privacy.md:267 (On this device) and privacy-policy.md:16 name the session copy of your UTxOs but not the spenders; architecture.md:148 and :419 do name them.

Severity is low. It is a narrower window of gap-g9#1, which review-51.md:194 rates medium→low. Only the user's own second profile plus a lock causes it (who: nobody). When it happens, the harm is gap-g9#1's: the test's stealth mint spends the other profile's session change (fb…#2) instead of the 400 ₳ received (e3…#0). The unqualified docs lines make this a claim wider than the code until the code is fixed or the lines are qualified.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Pick one. The first keeps the decision's "no record".

(A) Recommended: note arrivals at the read that seals the cursor past the spend. No new data is kept and no policy entry is needed.
- Add `activity?: Pick<ActivityService, "arrived">` to ScanDeps (contract-scan.ts:52). The deps that ScriptSpendDeps, BalanceDeps and the sessions, send and transfer services pass already carry `activity`.
- In readIndexView's first withKeys turn (:289-292), also take `phrasePin(phraseOf(keys))`. That is e4a#1's pin rule.
- After the final turn (:387-415), when this answer's `spentBy` names a spend at or below the new cursor (that is, :384 just sealed the cursor past it), call `deps.activity?.arrived(network, view.owned, pin, view.spentBy).catch(() => undefined)`.
- balances.ts:304 and :435 then find nothing fresh and return at activity.ts:541.
- Kept.spentBy and withSpentBy become redundant. Dropping them also settles the privacy.md question.
- flows.md:110 "noted from the balance reading" becomes "...or from the read that takes in another profile's spend". architecture.md:148 says the same.

(B) Seal the pairs.

findings.title: pending.ts still writes the Seedelf history unpinned when a maybe-sent payment settles, and since gap-g8#2 that includes a public Send's own-Seedelf entry
findings.scenario:

pending.ts:850 `if (w.summary) await deps.activity?.sent(w.network, shown(seen), w.summary).catch(() => undefined);`
pending.ts:939 `if (summary) await deps.activity?.sent(w.network, shown(current), summary).catch(() => undefined);`

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds. I traced it on HEAD (69d001e8) and reproduced it in a copy: the two new tests below fail on HEAD and pass once the pin is passed.

How it happens:
- **The pin.** settleNow takes it at pending.ts:833 (`const pin = phrasePin(); await wallet.withKeys(pin);`). Every pinned turn calls `pin(keys)`, at :842, :878, :919, :936, :948 and :977.
- **The two unpinned writes.**
  - :850 runs once the turn at :840-849 has passed: `if (w.summary) await deps.activity?.sent(w.network, shown(seen), w.summary).catch(() => undefined);`
  - :939 runs after the pinned dropKept: `if (summary) await deps.activity?.sent(w.network, shown(current), summary).catch(() => undefined);`
  - Neither passes `pin`, though it's in scope at both.
- **Where the summary comes from.** A public Send reaches settleNow with its summary: script-spend.ts:445 `submitWatched({... summary ...})`, then writeAhead's record (`summary: s.summary`, pending.ts:656), then stillMaybeSent. That summary carries `payments[].seedelf.own: true` and `origin: madePrivate(from)` (send.ts:185-186, :199).
- **What gets written.** activity.ts:353-375 is the new `kind === "send"` branch of sent(). It writes a move-in through `this.update(..., pin)`, and with pin undefined it skips both of update()'s checks (activity.ts:766, :776). store.get and store.set (private-store.ts:136-158) then go through withStoreKey, which seals under whatever phrase is loaded when the queue runs.
- **No guard found.** Remove (wallet.ts:504-511) doesn't touch ActivityService's queue. landedDeposit (lovejoin.ts:6940) and told (parts.ts settledPart) only match by txHash inside the current phrase's records, so neither leaks.
- **These are the only two left.** Every other history writer passes its pin: balances.ts:304 and :435 (e4a#1's residue, fixed this round), pending.ts:603 (`pinned`), dapp.ts:2300, sessions.ts:5370, :5403 and :5647 (turnPin), and lovejoin.ts:8173 and :8294.
- **Since when.** At 984ff48f, sent() returned at `!SEEDELF_KINDS.has(pending.kind)` for "send" (SEEDELF_KINDS, activity.ts:248-258, has no "send"). So before gap-g8#2 a Send wrote nothing there. The :850 and :939 calls are unchanged since 2b3dfd80, so Seedelf kinds settled after maybe-sent (transfer, withdraw, move-in and the rest) had the same gap already.
- **A comment overclaims.** The comment at :830-832 says that after a Remove and another phrase's restore, "nothing of it goes into that phrase's watch, reading or history". That's wider than the code.
- **Not decided anywhere.** DECISIONS.md and round1.json say nothing about these two calls.

**Reproduced:**
1. Wallet A (12-word phrase) makes a public Send of 50 ₳ to its own Seedelf "web-wallet". Koios takes the submit but the answer is lost, so it's maybe sent and nothing is written yet.
2. Home's look settles it. The history write is held, the way remove-wallet-reading.test.ts holds arrived().
3. reset-wallet (force), then restore-wallet with the 24-word phrase B.
4. On release, B's sealed private history contains A's entry: `{kind:"move-in", lovelace:"50000000", fee:"178349", origin:{id:"public:0",origin:"own"}, bySend:true, txHash:<A's>}`.

This happens on both paths, :850 (seen on chain) and :939 (sent again and taken). The control (no phrase change) passes and writes the move-in, so the fix doesn't break the normal case.

**Severity: low.** Only the user's own Remove and restore can cause it, and only in the short gap between the settle's last pinned turn and the history queue's next storage call. It's the same window e4a#1's residue was fixed for in arrived(). The harm is another phrase's amount, hash and an account class sealed into the new phrase's private Activity and CSV, until 500 newer entries push it out. No money is involved.

findings.title: If decodeTx fails, the window drops the metadata-hash warning, the register-on-chain warning and the own-Seedelf note without saying anything; a site can force it with one trailing byte
findings.scenario: A site's signTx sends `<tx>` with one byte appended (`<tx>00`). The body's auxiliary_data_hash commits to metadata M2. The transaction carries M1, a CIP-20 note such as "Swap 10 ADA for 20 MIN". Output 1 pays the user's own Seedelf under a register copied as found, or under a fresh d (no copy rule catches that one). WebAssembly's inspect reads and signs the first item: check_nesting stops at that item's end, Pallas's decode_fragment is minicbor::decode, which ignores what follows, and build::tx_id hashes only the body. The worker's decoded() gets decodeTx's "it has bytes after its end" (decode.rs:657) and returns undefined. The window then shows M1's note with no dapp-metadata-hash warning and no dapp-seedelf-on-chain warning. On Sign, notePrivate returns at `!detail`. The site strips the byte and submits with M2: the user signed metadata the window didn't show. The own-Seedelf output later reads as a payment received, which the next funding or stealth mint takes first, tying it to the public account in the open (gap-g1#2's harm, by default). Only Transaction details, if opened, says the wallet can't read the transaction. A second lever needs no extra byte and is a valid encoding: a redeemer key written `9f 00 00 ff` in the unsigned witness set (sign#2).
findings.evidence: dapp.ts:2215-2220 `const detail = this.decoded(network, (tx as string).trim()); ... if (detail?.metadataHashMatches === false) summary = { ...summary, metadataMismatch: true }; if (detail && (await this.registerOnChain(network, detail))) summary = { ...summary, registerOnChain: true };`. decoded() at :2239-2244: `try { return JSON.parse(wasm.decodeTx(net, txCbor)) as TxDetail; } catch (e) { if (isTrap(e)) throw e; return undefined; }`. notePrivate at :2279-2281: `const detail = activity ? this.decoded(network, txCbor) : undefined; ... if (!activity || !detail || !paid.length) return;`. wasm/src/decode.rs:655-657: `match whole.skip() { Ok(()) if whole.position() == bytes.len() => {} Ok(()) => bail!("... it has bytes after its end.")`. In contrast wasm/src/cip30.rs:1281-1284 (`check_nesting(&bytes)?; let tx = conway::Tx::decode_fragment(&bytes)...; let tx_hash = build::tx_id(&bytes)?;`) and seedelf-core/src/cbor.rs:195-235 (nests_within returns true once its first item closes) never check the end. The docs claim more than this: flows.md:432 "The window checks that metadata against the hash the body signs and, where they differ ... warns above the note"; architecture.md:213 "from the decode the worker makes of every request it reads"; privacy.md:341-342; privacy-policy.md:93 ("When you sign a site's transaction that pays your own Seedelf, the wallet now notes..."). Only x1a#3's line fails safe (`!detail` sets otherMetadata). No test covers a decode failure (dapp-metadata-hash, dapp-register-on-chain).
findings.fix: Take all three readings from WebAssembly's own read of the bytes it signs. (1) inspect refuses bytes after the transaction's end, as decode_tx does. The node refuses them too, so this is no new refusal. (2) TxSummary gets metadata_mismatch, computed in inspect from the `minted` it already decodes (raw auxiliary bytes against body.auxiliary_data_hash, sharing decode.rs's metadata_hash_matches). If `minted` fails to decode, it counts as a mismatch. (3) Paid carries each contract output's register points, output index and script flag, so registerOnChain reads summary.paid and notePrivate reads signed.summary.paid, never a second decoder. At the very least, readTx should fail closed: `if (!detail) summary = { ...summary, metadataMismatch: true }`.
findings.owner_question: Is refusing a transaction with bytes after its end acceptable under 'refuse only what the ledger refuses'? The node refuses such bytes too.

verdicts.evidence:
I traced this on HEAD (75956e22) from start to end and ran it through the real worker and WebAssembly. The pkg was built at 17:16, after the last Rust commit at 17:07. The finding holds as written, and I found no guard that stops it.

Path of `<tx>00` through signTx:
- dapp.ts:2335 `txBytes` checks only that it is hex and within the length limit. cbor.ts:131-150 `bodyField`/`bodyOutpoints` and :157 `certificateKinds` read the body and never look at the end. (The worker's `nestsWithin`, cbor.ts:106, does check the end, but signTx never calls it. Its only callers are dapp.ts:2039 and :2877.)
- WebAssembly `inspect` (cip30.rs:1280-1284): `check_nesting` → `nests_within` (core cbor.rs:195) starts with `Items(Some(1))` and returns true once that first item closes. `conway::Tx::decode_fragment` is `pallas_codec::minicbor::decode` (pallas-primitives-0.35.1 framework.rs:21-22 → minicbor-0.25.1 lib.rs:171-175 `Decoder::new(b).decode()`), which never checks for bytes left over. `build::tx_id` (build.rs:1269-1278) hashes only the body. `sign_tx` (cip30.rs:2129) runs the same inspect and signs that tx_hash.
- `decode_tx` (decode.rs:652-659) bails with "it has bytes after its end". `decoded()` (dapp.ts:2236-2245) catches that. It is a plain JsError, not a trap (wasm.ts:46), so `decoded()` returns undefined.
- readTx at dapp.ts:2215-2220: `otherMetadata` fails safe (`!detail`). `detail?.metadataHashMatches === false` is false and `detail && registerOnChain` is skipped, so neither warning shows.
- notePrivate at dapp.ts:2278-2281 returns at `!detail`.
- Nothing else on the path throws. `remember` uses `outputsOf`, which catches errors (dapp.ts:3055-3063). `siteSigned` falls back to the summary (sessions.ts:2749-2765). `ties` is caught.
- Only Transaction details (handlers.ts:431 waitingCbor → tx-view.ts:195 decodeTx) says it can't read the transaction.

All three checks were added in this round (git diff 984ff48f..HEAD of dapp.ts: besideNote → decoded, plus metadataMismatch, registerOnChain and notePrivate). DECISIONS' G5's notes asks for "Decode whenever the body could commit to metadata". x1a#2 asks to warn where the kept view holds the register. gap-g1#2 asks to note the outputs "since a site may submit the transaction itself".

The docs claim more than the code does:
- flows.md:432: "The window checks that metadata against the hash the body signs ... warns"
- architecture.md:213: "from the decode the worker makes of every request it reads"
- privacy.md:341-342
- privacy-policy.md:29 ("so that money is never taken for a payment received") and :93

No dapp test covers a trailing byte or a failed decode (grep).

Run results:
- Without the byte, the same transaction warns (metadataMismatch, registerOnChain).
- With it, the txHash is the same, the window shows the note "Swap 10 ADA for 20 MIN", and there is no warning.
- The wallet's ed25519 witness verifies (node:crypto) over the id of the stripped transaction carrying COMMITTED, and decodeTx of that transaction gives metadataHashMatches=true and note "I agree to pay 500 ADA".
- The own-Seedelf output is classed `received:<id>` and listed "Received", and the stealth mint spends `<id>#0` ahead of Bob's payment.

Why medium: a site turns off three of this round's fixes with one byte. The gap-g1#2 half becomes a privacy link the wallet's default coin pick makes: the public account is tied to the next stealth mint or funding in the open. The docs and the store privacy policy claim more than the code. Not high: no value is taken or misdirected, the metadata half is G5's harm, which moves no value, and the window still shows otherMetadata's line, "It carries other metadata too, which anyone can read." The underlying items were rated low or note-level in review-51.md (x1a#2 low, gap-g1#2 low, G5's notes (2) unrated).

I did not verify sign#2's second lever (a redeemer key written `9f 00 00 ff`).
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. Refuse bytes after the end in WebAssembly's `inspect` (cip30.rs:1281, after `check_nesting`), using decode.rs:652-659's check: `let mut whole = minicbor::Decoder::new(&bytes); match whole.skip() { Ok(()) if whole.position() == bytes.len() => {}, Ok(()) => bail!("The wallet can't read this transaction: it has bytes after its end."), Err(e) => bail!("The wallet can't read this transaction: {e}") }`.
   - Factor it into one helper that decode_tx, inspect and attach_witnesses (cip30.rs:2278) all call.
   - Don't change core's `check_nesting`: the CLI and other callers use it.
   - The "The wallet can't read" prefix already maps to APIError.InvalidRequest (dapp.ts:2185).
   - Answer to the owner's question: yes, this fits "refuse only what the ledger refuses". `<tx>00` is two CBOR items, not CIP-30's `cbor<transaction>`, and the node's decoder refuses leftover bytes. decode_tx and attach_witnesses already refuse them.
   - On its own this closes only this lever. sign#2 says a valid encoding also fails decode_tx, so refusing every decode failure would break the owner's rule. Steps 2 and 3 are the fix for the whole class.

2. Compute the metadata check in `inspect` from the `minted` it already decodes (cip30.rs:1371). Compare blake2b-256 of the raw auxiliary bytes with `body.auxiliary_data_hash`, sharing decode.rs's `metadata_hash_matches`. A hash with no metadata, or metadata with no hash, is a mismatch, and so is `minted` failing to decode. Add `metadata_mismatch` to TxSummary, and have dapp.ts take it from WebAssembly in place of `detail?.metadataHashMatches`.

3. Give each contract output in `paid` its register points, its output index and its reference-script flag. Then:
   - `registerOnChain(network, summary.paid)` reads those.
   - `notePrivate(network, holder, signed.summary, account)` reads `signed.summary.paid`, from the same bytes that were signed.
   - Drop `decoded()` from the signing path. Keep it, at most, for `moreThanNote`, which already fails safe, or move that check into inspect too.

Stopgap if 2 and 3 wait: in readTx, `if (!detail && summary.metadata) summary = { ...summary, metadataMismatch: true }`. That still leaves registerOnChain and the note open, so the docs would stay too wide: flows.md:432, architecture.md:213, privacy.md:341-342, privacy-policy.md:29/:93.

Tests:
- Add a trailing-byte case to dapp-metadata-hash.test.ts, dapp-register-on-chain.test.ts and site-payment-own-seedelf.test.ts. The test below shows each one.
- Add a Rust test that `inspect_tx` refuses `<tx>00`.
- Once 2 and 3 land, add a decode failure that isn't a trailing byte (sign#2's redeemer key).

THE CODE DOESN'T DO WHAT WAS DECIDED
DECISIONS.md says, per item:
- G5's notes: warn "when the note isn't the transaction's".
- x1a#2: warn where the kept view holds the register.
- gap-g1#2: note the payment at signTx.

The docs claim each of these without condition:

- architecture.md:213 says "from the decode the worker makes of every request it reads".
- privacy.md:341-342 says the payment "is noted ... as you sign it".

IMPACT
- Who can reach it: only a connected site, on purpose, for free. No honest builder appends bytes, and the site strips the byte before it submits. The metadata-hash and register warnings only matter against a hostile site, and that site can always do this, so the round's two warnings protect nothing against the one party they target.
- What's lost: no ADA. Every figure in the window comes from the bytes that get signed. What is lost:
  1. The user's signature publishes metadata other than the note shown, or metadata when the window showed none, with no warning. That's the state before G5's notes, which the review graded a note.
  2. The "anyone can see whose Seedelf" warning is missing. The words the window does show stay true.
  3. A payment into the user's own Seedelf under a fresh d is read as received (activity.ts:556-575). A funding then takes it at rank 1 instead of Own's 4, and a stealth mint at rank 1 (after a Lovejoin box) instead of 3 (build.rs:2484-2500). That publicly ties the new session or Seedelf to the public account, which is a link the wallet makes by default. The co-spending notes then say "a payment you received".
- What catches it later:

  - Transaction details says "can't read ... bytes after its end", but only if the user opens it.
- Grade: medium on the brief's scale. It is a claim wider than the code (four docs, the policy row and entry) and a privacy link made by default. It isn't high: no funds move, and the metadata mismatch was graded a note when it was decided. Graded by loss alone it would be low, since each of the three harms it reopens (gap-g1#2, x1a#2, G5's notes) was low or a note.
- Owner question: refusing the bytes after the end fits "refuse only what the ledger refuses". From knowledge: the node's decoder rejects leftover bytes. decode_tx and attach_witnesses (cip30.rs:2278-2279) already refuse them.

findings.title: Two readers of a site's transaction still read inner arrays as fixed-length (decode.rs redeemers(), cbor.ts outpoints()), so valid transactions are refused or can't be shown (gap-g8#5's class)
findings.scenario: (a) A site's Plutus transaction writes its redeemer map key as `9f 00 00 ff` ([_ spend, 0]), or holds two redeemers with an open-length (indefinite) ex_units. Pallas reads it: minicbor-derive 0.15.3 reads an array of either length to its break. The ledger's decodeRecordNamed does too (inferred, not checked here). decode.rs reads the array head, then the next head lands on the break: "a redeemer isn't readable". Transaction details, in the window and in Activity, can't show this valid transaction. Through sign#1, the window's metadata and register checks and the own-Seedelf note also go silent, with no byte appended. The witness set isn't signed, so the site can write it this way at will. (b) A site's transaction spends two of the account's UTxOs, the first input written `[_ txid, 0]`. cbor.ts outpoints() sets p to the pair's break, then reads the second input from it ("5820#…"). resolve never fetches the real second row, and WebAssembly refuses: "spends a UTxO the wallet can't find yet". The same misread in spent.ts rememberSiteSpent records a garbage outpoint after a submitTx, so the spent input stays in getUtxos until Koios catches up.
findings.evidence: decode.rs:1449-1454 `let ex_units = |d| { d.array().map_err(unreadable)?; let mem = d.u64()...; let steps = d.u64()...; Ok((mem, steps)) };`. :1466-1469 `d.array().map_err(unreadable)?; let tag = d.u64()...; let index = d.u64()...; d.array().map_err(unreadable)?;`. The returned count is dropped and no break is ever read. cbor.ts:207-211 `const id = head(b, head(b, p).p); const index = head(b, id.p + id.n); found.push(...); p = index.p;`. decode.rs is unchanged this round, but the window now relies on it for every request. The fixer's note says "A site's transaction written with indefinite lengths is read as the ledger reads it"; only the outer list, the body map and cip30.rs's witness-set readers were made to read either length.
findings.fix: In redeemers(), keep each inner array's count. When it's open-length, read up to and consume its break, with a small helper like cip30.rs's at_end. In cbor.ts outpoints(), step over each pair with `p = skip(b, p, 3)` and read id and index inside it, whatever its length. Add both shapes to cbor-indefinite.test.ts and decode_test.rs.

(a) decode.rs redeemers()
- seedelf-web-wallet/wasm/src/decode.rs:1466-1469 reads the key with `d.array()`, `d.u64()`, `d.u64()`, then calls `d.array()` for the value. :1493 does the same for a list-form record, and the ex_units closure at :1449-1453 too. Each count is dropped and no break is ever read.

  - The Conway redeemer key is `deriving via CBORGroup` (Scripts.hs:236-246), whose decoder is `groupRecord = decodeRecordNamed` (Group.hs:33-35).
  - A list-form record is `decodeRecordNamed "Redeemer"` (TxWits.hs:607-613).

D decNat` (ExUnits.hs:208-212). `decodeCount (RecD cn) n = decodeRecordNamed "RecD" (const n) (pure (n, cn))` (Coders.hs:482) checks for the break before the fields, so an open-length ex_units fails with "Excess terms in array". The map value is `decodeTuple` = `decodeListLenOf 2` (DecCBOR.hs:297-302). The ledger refuses both today, so decode.rs refusing two redeemers with an open ex_units agrees with it.

  - With the key `9f 00 00 ff`, Pallas reads 1 redeemer, but decode_tx returns Err("a redeemer isn't readable: unexpected type break at position 4: expected array").

An open list whose first record is open-length shows 1 redeemer where Pallas reads 2: minicbor's skip() eats the record's break as the list's (minicbor-0.25.1 decoder.rs:560-568), so the second redeemer is silently dropped.
- Effect: Transaction details (tx-view.ts:195) throws.
- Effect in the window, through sign#1: dapp.ts decoded() (:2236-2245) returns undefined. Then :2219 sets no metadataMismatch, :2220's registerOnChain needs `detail`, and notePrivate returns at :2281.

A trailing byte alone also opens the window unwarned (tested): inspect's `conway::Tx::decode_fragment` (cip30.rs:1282) ignores trailing bytes, and the worker doesn't check for them (dapp.ts:3121). This shape is the route that survives a sign#1 fix that only aligns the two readers on trailing bytes.

(b) cbor.ts outpoints()

Who can cause it: a site. On its own, sign#2 is a valid but exotic transaction refused or not shown, plus a spent input not remembered: low. The window silencing it feeds is sign#1's to rate, but it has to be fixed together with this.

findings.title: A second page of the site joins the shared connect question only after three awaits, so the first page leaving in between turns the site away
findings.scenario: Tab A of https://dex.example asks to connect, and the window shows its question. Tab B of the same site loads and calls enable(). B waits in needsPassword(), then in site(), a sealed read on the wallet's queue that can sit behind a balance reading for seconds, then in lovejoinRoomKept(). Meanwhile the user closes tab A. gone(A) finds no live sharer (sharedBy is still empty) and no unlock wait from the origin, so it calls refuseFor(origin). B then finds no question and `refusing(origin)` is true, so B hears "declined just now, ask again in 10 s". B was about to wait on that very question, which is the owner's B7 exception, and before this round it would have asked itself.
findings.evidence: enable(): `const password = await this.needsPassword(); ... const site = await this.site(network, origin); ... const room = !site && (await this.deps.sessions.lovejoinRoomKept(network)); const asking = this.waiting.find(...); if (asking) { const sharers = (asking.sharedBy ??= new Set()); sharers.add(session.id);` (dapp.ts:1102-1120). gone(): `const shared = [...(question?.sharedBy ?? [])].some(live) || this.unlocking.some((u) => u.session.origin === session.origin); if (!shared) this.refuseFor(...)` (:917-919).
findings.fix: Count a page as a sharer from enable()'s first line. Add its session id to a per-origin set of enable() calls in flight before the first await, and remove it in a finally. gone() then treats a live page in that set as a sharer, just as sharedBy does. Add a dapp-gone case where tab A goes while tab B's site() read is held.

verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD 69d001e8 (the fixes tree, untouched; git status is clean). The finding holds, and the race window is wider than it says.

How it happens:
1. Tab A asks, so its connect entry is in `waiting`. Tab B of the same origin (its own port, so its own session id, sw.ts:370) calls enable().
2. B is first counted as a sharer at dapp.ts:1119-1120 (`const sharers = (asking.sharedBy ??= new Set()); sharers.add(session.id);`). Every await between call()'s entry and that line is a gap where it isn't counted yet:
   - in call(): :580 `await this.readRefusals()`
   - in run(): :597 `await this.deps.preferences.get()`, :602 `await this.deps.wallet.state()` (wallet.ts:271 `return this.serial(() => this.load())`, which waits on the wallet's queue), :607 `await this.unlocked(...)` while locked, :611 `await this.deps.network()`
   - in enable(): :1102 `await this.needsPassword()`, :1104 `await this.site(network, origin)` (it reaches PrivateStore.get, private-store.ts:138 `this.deps.wallet.withStoreKey(...)`, the same queue), :1114 `await this.deps.sessions.lovejoinRoomKept(network)`.
3. The user closes A. sw.ts:433-435 calls gone(A) from the port's disconnect, synchronously and in a task of its own, so it can land between any of those awaits.
4. gone(A) at :914-919 (`const shared = [...(question?.sharedBy ?? [])].some(live) || this.unlocking.some((u) => u.session.origin === session.origin); if (!shared) this.refuseFor(...)`) finds sharedBy undefined. With the wallet unlocked, `unlocking` is empty, so it calls refuseFor(origin).
5. B resumes and finds no `asking`, because A's entry was removed at :912. Then :1133-1135 (`if (this.refusing(origin)) { this.askedAgain(origin); throw refused(this.declinedWait(origin)); }`).
6. Locked variant: A waits in `unlocking`, and B is still before unlocked()'s push (:1587). gone(A) finds no unlocking from the origin and refuses, and B is refused at :1571 with the same words.

No guard covers it. pageCalls and gonePages track B's call, but gone() never looks at other pages' running calls. At 984ff48f gone() had no refuseFor, so B asked itself. DECISIONS, G6's note (OWNER B7 = (a)), says "except when another page of the same site waits on that question", and B, called while A's question was up, was about to wait on it.

Reachability: in Chrome each of those awaits is a chrome.storage round trip or a turn of the wallet's serial queue.
- With the wallet idle, the window is a few milliseconds.
- During a contract scan, each queue turn can wait one batch (contract-scan.ts:136-137, OWNED_BATCH = 200, "a few hundred milliseconds on a slow machine"). B takes two turns (state(), withStoreKey), so the window is up to about a second. The finding's "seconds" is the generous end.

Cost:
- B hears {code -3, "The user declined this site just now. It can ask again in 10 s."}.
- askedAgain marks the refusal retried, and the site is listed as declined on the dApps page and Connected sites.
- The refusal counts in a row, so the next one within the reset is 1 min.
- Way out: wait 10 s, or press Let it ask now. No funds are involved.
- Who: nobody, beyond the user's own timing; a site gains nothing. Low, as the finding says.

Test run, on a copy of HEAD:
- (a) B held in enable()'s site() sealed read, (b) B held at the wallet's queue before enable() is entered, and (c) the unlock-wait variant all fail. B hears DECLINED_WAIT and the site is listed as declined.
- The control, B already at the sharing branch when A leaves, passes.
- With gone()'s refuseFor switched off, which is the pre-round behaviour, all four pass.
- With a prototype of the fix below, all four pass, and so do dapp-gone, dapp-enable, dapp-declined, dapp-caps, dapp-prompt, dapp-approvals-locked, dapp, dapp-funding-queue, dapp-governance and dapp-reach (11 files, 161 tests).

What holds, checked: the rest of the G6 rule works as decided.
- A page that leaves its question with no other page waiting is refused.
- A site is refused once every sharer has gone (in the order second, then first).
- A sharer already at the branch asks itself.
- Signatures, a sent funding and a governance-only question are not counted.
- A wait for the unlock that another page still shares is not counted.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. Register in call(), not in enable(). The finding's sketch, "from enable()'s first line", is not enough: run() awaits preferences.get(), wallet.state() (the same wallet queue as the sealed read) and, while locked, unlocked()'s own state() and network() before enable() is entered. Cases (b) and (c) below still fail with that version.
   - In call() (dapp.ts:573-594), when `method === "enable"`, count the page in a new `private readonly enabling = new Map<string, Map<string, number>>()` (origin, then session id, then a count). Do it before `await this.readRefusals()`, and decrement in the existing finally, deleting empty entries.
   - Use a count, not a Set. One page often calls enable() several times at once (dapp-enable.test.ts "called enable() more than once"), and the first call's finally would drop the page while its other calls still run.
2. In gone() (:916-919), add `|| [...(this.enabling.get(session.origin)?.keys() ?? [])].some(live)` to `shared`.
   - `live` already excludes the leaving page's own id and pages in gonePages, so a page's own repeated calls still don't count, and "turns it away once every page that shared the question has gone" still passes.
   - The new map covers everything sharedBy does, since every sharer's enable() is still running. Keep sharedBy, or drop it to have one mechanism.
   - The same change covers the unlock-wait race (c).
3. The prototype is about 12 lines in call() plus one clause in gone(). It passed the four race cases and the 11 dApp test files (161 tests).
4. Add cases (a), (b) and (c) from the test field to dapp-gone.test.ts's "chunk 51, G6's note" describe:
   - (a) hold `t.store.get` for "dapps", so B waits in site()
   - (b) hold the wallet's queue with `t.wallet.withKeys(() => gate)`, so B waits at run()'s state()
   - (c) hold `t.preferences.get` with the wallet locked while A leaves its wait for the unlock.

findings.title: A box brought back unmixed is classed as a Lovejoin box, so the stealth mint (and a private pool start) now spends it first
findings.scenario: The user's private Mix (session 4) stops after its deposit: a lock, or giveme.my refusing the mix. Its box sits there not mixed. The user presses Bring one back anyway, whose warning only says the deposit gets tied to the private balance. Three other paths end the same way: a private Bootstrap's box brought back by hand, a private Bootstrap's released boxes that nobody has mixed, and the retired pools' run (1.8.0 on), which brings unmixed boxes back by itself. withdrawOne writes no origin for such a box, because depositAccountOf returns undefined for a session's chain. So its history reads boxFrom(withdraw), origin "lovejoin", the same as a mixed box. Later the user creates a Seedelf from the private balance. Purpose::Mint now ranks Lovejoin 0 (B15 (b)), and step 1 takes the smallest single UTxO that pays alone by rank, so it spends that unmixed box. On chain the trail runs: mint, then the withdraw, the box, the deposit, the one-time account, the funding, then the user's private UTxOs (and the public account, for money made private). Meanwhile the mint note says "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account". A pool start paid from the private balance uses Purpose::Mint too. e1a#1's decision (4) relied on "its box:<tx> class ranks after received money", which B15 (b) reversed. The stranger's case was fixed (receivedIn), but the user's own unmixed boxes weren't. G4a1 named this residual for G1a/G6a (notes.txt, G4a1 note 3), and nobody changed it. Histories already hold such entries from 1.8.x retired-pool runs and earlier Bring one back anyway presses.
findings.who: user, through ordinary steps (Bring one back anyway or a Bootstrap's box, then Create a Seedelf from the private balance); nobody needs to act for boxes the retired pools' run already brought back
findings.evidence: lovejoin.ts:8085-8086 `const own = received ? receivedIn(built.txHash) : boxFrom(built.txHash);` / `origin = spent || received ? merged([own, ...]) : undefined;` (undefined for an own unmixed box paying itself). lovejoin.ts:2364 `if (chain) return chain.session === undefined ? (chain.account ?? 0) : undefined;` (no tie for a session's deposit). activity.ts:797-798 `case "lovejoin-withdraw": return boxFrom(entry.txHash);`. build.rs:2484-2486 `Purpose::Mint => match class.origin { Lovejoin => 0, Received => 1,`. en.json mint.privacy.fromPrivate: "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account." DECISIONS e1a#1 (4): "its box:<tx> class ranks after received money".
findings.fix: In withdrawOne, when the box isn't known to be mixed at that point, merge boxFrom with the class of whatever put it in, so REACH names it session or unknown and Mint ranks it 4 or 2, after received money. 'Not known to be mixed' covers boxes in notMixedYet, unsure or untold of the schedule as read, a Bootstrap's held or released box nobody mixed, and a retired pool's box that mixedOf doesn't vouch for. Use sessionClass(n) where a session's chain or mix entry made it, and unknownIn(tx) where the maker isn't known. Public ones keep their tie as today. Entries already written carry no marker. Either rank box: first for Mint only on entries that carry a mixed mark written from now on, or state the gap in privacy.md's Creating a Seedelf and in the mint note.
findings.owner_question: For Lovejoin entries already in users' histories (1.8.x retired-pool runs, earlier Bring one back anyway, Bootstrap boxes), which can't be told from mixed boxes without a lookup: should the stealth mint rank only boxes marked mixed from now on first, or accept and say so?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD (69d001e8). I traced it end to end, and a test in a copy of the tree confirms it.

How the value flows:
1. lovejoin.ts:2362-2367, depositAccountOf: `if (chain) return chain.session === undefined ? (chain.account ?? 0) : undefined;`. A mix entry is handled the same way. So a session's deposit (a private Mix, a private Bootstrap) gets no tie.
2. lovejoin.ts:8075: `received = someoneElses(...)`. someoneElsesOf (:2671-2675) only looks at depositsOf boxes, which are boxes no record accounts for. It also drops any deposit whose inputs include one of the phrase's one-time keys. So `received` is false for the wallet's own session deposits, whether a chain record has them or Koios said so after a restore.
3. lovejoin.ts:8085-8086: `const own = received ? receivedIn(built.txHash) : boxFrom(built.txHash);` then `origin = spent || received ? merged([...]) : undefined;`. The result is undefined. At :8171, `...(origin ? { origin } : tiedOrigin(built.txHash, ties))` adds nothing, because ties is undefined unless the public account paid.
4. activity.ts:785-798, classOf: `case "lovejoin-withdraw": return boxFrom(entry.txHash);`, which gives origin "lovejoin".
5. build.rs:2484-2486: `Purpose::Mint => match class.origin { Lovejoin => 0, Received => 1,`. In step 1 (:2827-2831, one_more :2722), candidates sort by (last, rank) and then by lovelace. So an unmixed box that pays alone is spent first.
6. Purpose::Mint is used by the stealth mint (wasm lib.rs:2490) and by a pool start (lib.rs:2801).

What the round's own words claim:
- en.json:1464, changed this round from "Only money others paid you…" to "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account."
- privacy.md:107: a box back from Lovejoin "hides the payer from people reading the chain… No payer knows a box back from a mix, so a box that pays alone goes first".
- privacy.md:81 and :172.
- architecture.md:137: "a box back from Lovejoin, which no payer knows".
- build.rs:2460-2463 (the Purpose::Mint doc comment).

The anyway warning (en.json:998) only says "anyone can tie your deposit to your private balance".

The behaviour is pinned, not decided:
- G4a1's own test pins it: lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:256-257 `expect((await historyOf(t, own.txHash))?.origin).toBeUndefined();`.
- G4a1's note 3 flagged it. G1a's entry says "left: Nothing". The owner's B15 line decided boxes "no payer knows"; nobody decided this case.

Existing histories:
- web-wallet/1.8.0 and 1.9.1 have the same `origin = spent ? … : undefined` and the same session branch in depositAccountOf. So histories written by the retired pools' run, Bring every box back and Bring one back anyway already hold box:<tx> for such boxes.
- In 1.9.1, Mint ranked Received 0 and Lovejoin 1, and such a box already came before Unknown, Own and Session money. What the round adds: it now comes before received money too, and the words now claim more than the code does.

Run in a copy (test below), both cases fail on HEAD:
- The withdraw entry has `origin: null`.
- classes gives `box:<tx>` with origin "lovejoin".
- The stealth mint spends only the unmixed box's way back, though Bob's 60 ₳ received would pay alone.
- copied-register-payment.test.ts, part (b) included, passed in the same run, so the WebAssembly package has the new ranks.

Checked and holds:
- A stranger's box comes back as receivedIn.
- A public account's deposit comes back tied to its account (origin "own").

Limits:
- A pool start takes such a box first only if the box pays the whole start alone. Step 2 skips classes that hold one UTxO, and merging takes boxes last (tier 2).
- The on-chain trail (mint → withdraw → box → deposit → one-time account → funding) is inferred from how a deposit is built. It was not run on chain.

Two flaws in the proposed fix:
- `mixedOf` vouches for every recorded box, deposit boxes included: `recorded` uses makers, which includes c.deposit (:1515, :2058-2063, :2085-2088). So "a box mixedOf doesn't vouch for" can't be the test for mixed.
- `merged([boxFrom, unknownIn])` still has origin "lovejoin". REACH (histories.ts:91) lists "lovejoin" before "unknown", and merged() (:101-106) takes REACH's first.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. withdrawOne (lovejoin.ts:8085-8086): decide inside the update, from `s` as read, whether the box is known to be mixed, then class its way back:
   (a) Someone else's box: receivedIn, as now.
   (b) A public account's deposit: as now (ties, then tiedOrigin, then "own").
   (c) A session's deposit that no mix has moved since: merged([boxFrom(tx), sessionClass(n)]). This gives origin "session": Mint ranks it 4, and a top-up of that same session ranks it 0. n comes from:
      - a chain whose c.deposit or c.tail?.deposit is box.txHash, with c.session set;
      - a mix entry's deposit (or e.id, for a Bootstrap or a seed), with e.session set;
      - after a restore, the index of the oneTime.keyHash(i) that matched in Origin.inputs. oneTimeKeys returns a Set today, so it would have to return key → index.
   (d) Not known to be mixed, with no known maker (notMixedYet, unsure or untold, a held or released Bootstrap box with no recorded session, or a retired pool's box that no record and no Koios answer says a mix made): use unknownIn(tx) alone.

2. Don't use mixedOf, recorded or knownOf as the test for "mixed": they count a chain's own deposit box as known. Use unmixedOf(s.chains, [box]), depositsOf, bootstrapOf, a deposit match against chains and mix entries, and the absence of a Koios answer.

3. Coverage: Bring one back anyway, Bring every box back now, the retired pools' run and withdrawDue (released Bootstraps) all call withdrawOne, so this one change covers them all. settleWithdrawing (:8282-8290) already passes w.origin through.

4. Tests:

   - I tried (c) and (d) as a prototype in the copy. The review test then passed, copied-register-payment stayed green, and only :257 failed, as expected.

5. Entries already written can't be told apart without a lookup. That's the finding's owner question. Until it's answered, or if the gap is accepted, reword en.json mint.privacy.fromPrivate (a critical key, so it needs the blind es/ja back-translation), privacy.md:81, :107 and :172, architecture.md:137 and build.rs:2460-2463. verdicts.evidence:
I traced this by reading the code on web-wallet/whole-review-fixes at 69d001e8, ran one existing test, and changed nothing in the tree. Every line the finding cites matches.

**How the box gets the wrong class**
- In withdrawOne (lovejoin.ts:8075-8086) only someoneElses changes the class: `const own = received ? receivedIn(built.txHash) : boxFrom(built.txHash);` then `origin = spent || received ? merged([...]) : undefined;`.
- depositAccountOf (lovejoin.ts:2364) has `if (chain) return chain.session === undefined ? (chain.account ?? 0) : undefined;`, so a session's deposit gets no tie. It also checks only `c.deposit`, never `c.tail.deposit` (makers, :1515), so it doesn't look up a session collateral's box at all.
- Take a box the wallet's own session deposited, that no mix moved, brought back paying its own way. It gets no origin and no ties: at :8171, `tiedOrigin(tx, undefined)` returns `{}`. Then classOf (activity.ts:797-798) gives `boxFrom`, origin "lovejoin". ActivityService.classes (activity.ts:467-500) re-classes only Received rows, so WebAssembly receives it as a Lovejoin box.

**The round's own test pins it**
- tests/lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:256-257 brings back anyway the box that one-time key 0 (session 0) deposited, then expects `origin` toBeUndefined().
- I ran it on this tree with `npx vitest run tests/lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts -t "the wallet's own deposit's as a box back from Lovejoin"`: 1 passed. The tree was still clean afterwards.

**How the mint picks it**
- In core, build.rs:2484-2486 has Mint ranking `Lovejoin => 0, Received => 1`.
- In step 1, `ranked` (:2830) feeds one_more, which sorts by `(rank, lovelace_of)` (:2725). So the smallest Lovejoin-class UTxO that pays alone goes first.
- mint_test's B15 test shows a 4 ₳ received UTxO pays a stealth mint alone, so a box back from a 5 ₳ pool (about 4.7 ₳) does too.
- The stealth mint (wasm lib.rs:2490) and the pool start (:2801) both use Purpose::Mint.

**Nothing later catches it**
- CreateSeedelf's review (:140-160) lists no inputs.
- historiesNote (histories.ts:188-235) writes its note only when `classes.length > 1` (:209), so a spend of one class shows nothing.
- The UTxOs screen tags the box "Back from Lovejoin", the same as a mixed one, so the user can't knowingly lock it out.

**Paths I confirmed in code**
- Bring one back anyway (withdrawNowNow, :7347+). Its warning, lovejoin.anyway.privacy.stopped or .deposit, says only that the deposit is tied to the private balance.
- A private Bootstrap's held box, and its released boxes.
- Bring every box back now (:7765).
- The retired pools' run (sortOut :6200-6203: "its boxes all come back, mixed or not"). It runs unasked once per network. It already wrote such entries in 1.8.x, and it does again for anyone updating from 1.7.x or earlier, or restoring with boxes in a retired pool.

**Words wider than the code**
- This round changed mint.privacy.fromPrivate (en.json:1464) to "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart…".
- privacy.md:81, :107 and :172 say a box back from Lovejoin hides the payer and goes first.

**The residual was named and left**
- G4a1 named it (notes.txt:35, note 3, and round1.json G4a1 "Named, not edited (G1a/G6a, B15's (b))").
- The round's only edit to the origin line in lovejoin.ts is e1a#1's received case.

**Impact**
- Who can reach it: only the user. A stranger's box now comes back as receivedIn, and no site is involved.
- What's lost: no ADA, but privacy. Anyone can tie the new Seedelf, or the pool start, to that deposit, the session's one-time account and its activity, the funding, and through the funding's inputs to where they came from. For money the user made private, that's the public account. The note says this money avoids exactly that.
- What the round changed: before it, Mint ranked Received 0 and Lovejoin 1. So where no received money paid alone, the wallet already picked this box over Unknown, Own and Session money. B15 (b) makes it beat received money too, and the new note claims it keeps the Seedelf apart.
- Reach is narrow. It needs an unmixed box of the user's own in the balance. Then it needs a Seedelf created from the private balance, which isn't the default while the account holds UTxOs (CreateSeedelf.tsx:64), or a pool start, which defaults to private (LovejoinLaunch.tsx:103). Every step is ordinary UI, though, and the retired pools' run creates the first condition without asking.
- Grade: medium. The wallet's own coin pick makes a privacy link, under a note that says it doesn't.

findings.title: The escape hatch re-asks in a loop, with no word why, while a box someone else's mix just moved sits in the pool
findings.scenario: Take a stuck token pool (cantComeBack), with the wallet on account 0. It holds A1, account 1's mixed leaf, known from its chain record. It also holds U, its own box that someone else's mix moved 20 minutes ago: no record, no origin, but a due time, so status asks nothing about it. On the page, U isn't in notMixed, unsure, bootstrap or reserved, so hatchAccountOf returns undefined and the question names nobody. In the worker, backOrder puts U last (early: it has waited less than the delay's least) and A1 first. A1 is known, so `force` is empty and U is never asked about. mixedOf(U) is false, so A1 is the only pick: whose=1, pressedOn=0, named undefined, so it throws AskAgainError. The page refreshes, gets the same status, and asks the same question naming nobody. Every press repeats this until U has waited the least (1 hour at Settings' default, longer for longer delays). Nothing is sent and nothing is lost, but the only way out of a stuck pool is a button that does nothing. The cause: the worker's picks (known-mixed, forced only ahead of the first known box) aren't what the page counts.
findings.who: nobody: ordinary pool traffic, any other user's mix moving one of the wallet's boxes
findings.evidence: lovejoin.ts:7401-7402 `const first = order.findIndex(known); force = first < 0 ? order : order.slice(0, first);`, :7433 `free(of(back), reserved).filter((b) => old.has(poolOf(b)) || mixed(b))`, :7464 `if (whose !== undefined && whose !== pressedOn && whose !== named) throw new AskAgainError(t("lj.boxReserved"));`. Lovejoin.tsx:1154 `const never = new Set([...pool.notMixed, ...(pool.unsure ?? []), ...(pool.bootstrap ?? []), ...(pool.reserved ?? [])]...)`, :3051-3054 `if (!isAskAgain(e)) throw e; await onRefresh(); setAsking({ paid: true }); return;`.
findings.fix: Have AskAgainError carry the account the worker would take (`whose`), pass it through ui-port's reply, and have the page ask again naming that account directly (PaidQuestion account and hatchRequest's `account` from the error, not from a re-read). Alternatively, in withdrawNowNow's paid path, force-ask every unknown box in the pool before settling on another account's box.

verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD (69d001e8) and reproduced with the real WebAssembly. Each press sends nothing and opens the same question again, with no line saying why. This lasts until U has waited the delay's least.

**Page side**
- status (lovejoin.ts:6706) calls sortOut with force=[].
- found() (6354-6379) asks Koios only when moreThanDue (6370) or for a forced box.
- In the steady state the due times cover every box. A stuck pool keeps its due times: withdrawDue pushes each one STUCK_WAIT_MS on (7207-7208). So U gets no origin and is in neither unsure nor notMixed.
- view() (6713-6747) gives boxes=[a1,U] and otherAccounts=[a1→1]. originOf(U) is undefined (2217-2222).
- hatchAccountOf (Lovejoin.tsx:1152-1158): the never set is empty, so accounts=[1, undefined]. `accounts.every(a => a !== undefined)` is false, so it returns undefined.
- PaidQuestion gets account={hatchAccountOf(pool)} (3814). hatchRequest leaves `account` out (1139-1142). hatchTakes is true (3305).

**Worker side**
- pressedOn=0 for both payers: `paid ? keys.account : undefined` (7361-7364), and "private" is truthy.
- No `box`, so order=backOrder(...)=[a1,U] (7400). U is early: waitedAt is block_time+least and is past now (2192, 2205). a1 is not early.
- `first = order.findIndex(known)` is 0, because a1's mix tx is in makers (1515, 2060). So `force = order.slice(0, first)` is [] (7401-7402) and U is never asked of.
- sortOut puts U in `back`. mixedOf(U) is false (2085-2088; mixedFor(undefined) returns undefined, 1251). So order=[a1] (7433).
- hatchOrder takes a1 (7436). whose=accountOf("public.1")=1 (7463). Since 1≠0 and 1≠undefined, it throws AskAgainError (7464).
- ui-port.ts:17 maps the error to askAgain. Lovejoin.tsx:3050-3054 runs onRefresh, then `setAsking({ paid: true })`. The fresh status is the same, because nothing looked U up. So the question names nobody again.

**Guards checked, none applies**
- Nothing in the paid path forces unknown boxes.
- rejudge (6516) only re-judges origins already kept. scheduleFound (5673) asks nobody.
- Both payer buttons loop.
- The comment at 7458-7462 says the page "asks again from a fresh read, which names it". That doesn't hold here. The fixer's gap-g2#2 notes in round1.json didn't consider this case.

**Root cause**
- The worker's forced lookup follows backOrder, but its pick follows hatchOrder.
- The page counts U under hatchOrder's own documented rule (2340-2345): another account's box is taken "only where nothing else is". U, which no public account put in, is there.
- At 984ff48f the worker would have sent a1, paid by account 0, after a question naming nobody. That is the R3-3 tie. The round's backstop (a) met the M14 forced-lookup rule and turned that tie into this loop.

**How long it lasts**
- Once U has waited the delay's least, early(U)=0 and own(U)=0 < own(a1)=1 (ownLeaves, 2392). U then comes first, is forced and asked of, and ranks 0 in hatchOrder, so U is sent.
- The least is 1 h at the default "1-6" (preferences.ts:175) and 6 h at "6-24". My second test confirms it: at +41 min the same unnamed request spends U and not a1.

**Severity: low**
- Who can cause it: nobody in particular; ordinary pool traffic does it.
- It needs a wallet whose second account mixed in a stuck token pool.
- Nothing is sent or lost. The button does nothing, temporarily, with no word why.
verdicts.fix_notes:
**Primary fix (worker).** It makes the worker match the page and hatchOrder's own rule. No new strings and no new kind of request.

In withdrawNowNow's no-box branch (lovejoin.ts:7400-7402), rank by hatchOrder before choosing what to force when the box is paid for:
```ts
const order = backOrder(free(of(owned).filter((b) => !held.has(ref(b))), reserved), rows, ownLeaves(before), least, this.deps.now());
const ranked = paid && pressedOn !== undefined ? hatchOrder(order, before, pressedOn) : order;
const first = ranked.findIndex(known);
force = first < 0 ? ranked : ranked.slice(0, first);
```
- A box no record names has originOf undefined, so it ranks 0 and is asked of ahead of another account's known box.
- Where the account on screen has a known box, that box still comes first and nothing extra is asked.
- Update the comment at 7388-7390 ("those backOrder puts ahead of the first whose making is known") to say hatchOrder's order when paid.

I tried this in a copy:
- The new test sends U at the first press, with one tx_info for U. That is the same M14 lookup the forced path already makes, through Koios alone. It's a request the policy already covers, so no Changes entry is needed.
- 344 tests across 11 related files pass: escape-hatch-reserved, lovejoin-crediting-review-fixes (including R3-3), lovejoin-flows, lovejoin, lovejoin-accounts, lovejoin-restore, lovejoin-bring-review-fixes, lovejoin-bring-screen-review-fixes, lovejoin-merged-review, lovejoin-reward-balance, lovejoin-release-rules.
- If Koios can't say of a forced box, the existing lj.untoldSomeMixed refusal says why.

**Optional backstop.** This covers any disagreement that is left, such as the state changing between the page's read and the press:
- Give AskAgainError the account: `new AskAgainError(msg, whose)`.
- Carry it in the reply: an `account?: number` beside `code` in shared/rpc.ts Reply, ui-port's answer, and a field on RpcError.
- In the page's `paid` handler, ask again naming that account: `setAsking({ paid: true, account })`. PaidQuestion and hatchRequest then take it from there instead of hatchAccountOf.

Don't ship the backstop alone. Here it would name account 1 and tie accounts 0 and 1 while U, which ties nobody, is there.

**The test.** Add tests/escape-hatch-unknown-ahead.test.ts (below). Both of its tests pass after the primary fix.

A finished chain is never marked CHAIN_CUT. tailChain still keys on `started`, so a cut tail resumes. intoPool, the Lovejoin branch, lovejoinWantsCollateral and the mixStopped write are all gated. class#1: definite_pairs refuses only what the node refuses (a general-form pair that isn't two items, malformed CBOR). A cancel carries and hashes the datum's own bytes.
