findings.title: 0.7.1 is a patch number on a release that breaks seedelf-core's public API since 0.7.0
findings.scenario: Once seedelf-core 0.7.1 is on crates.io, someone runs `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` without --locked, from a pinned script say. Cargo reads the published CLI's `seedelf-core = "0.7.0"` as ^0.7.0 and picks core 0.7.1. The build then fails with E0308: 0.7.0's balance.rs:37 calls `utxos::collect_all_wallet_utxos(scalar, &config.contract.seedelf_policy_id, every_utxo)`, and in 0.7.1 that argument is `contract: &Contract`. The same happens at sweep.rs:151, transfer.rs:102/112, fund.rs:103, remove.rs:55, find.rs:37, util/mint.rs:68 and statistics.rs:16. A crate depending on seedelf-core "0.7" breaks on `cargo update` the same way, and also through the new `orders::Protocol::SundaeSwapV4` variant (no #[non_exhaustive]) and the new `pub cant_come_back` field on `lovejoin::Launch`, whose fields are all public. Some changes don't break the build but change behaviour silently: a caller that guarded payments with `build::is_payable_address` now pays script addresses with no datum, and `launch`/`launch_apart` now return Ok for a pool whose boxes can't come back, where they used to refuse it. Once published, this can't be taken back: crates.io never overwrites a version, and yanking 0.7.1 would also hide the fixes from `cargo install seedelf-cli`.
findings.who: user (anyone installing the published 0.7.0 CLI by version, or building against seedelf-core 0.7); nobody malicious
findings.evidence: bd45ee21 sets `version = "0.7.1"` and `seedelf-core = "0.7.1"` (Cargo.toml:14-17, 28). Its own message gives the reason as "seedelf-core's public API, a published crate". 03cf290e's message says: "The six reader signatures in seedelf-core take the contract config in place of the policy id: breaking for the published crate (0.x)". Now utxos.rs:53 is `pub fn collect_all_wallet_utxos(sk: Scalar, contract: &Contract, utxos: Vec<UtxoResponse>)`. At tag 0.7.0, `git grep` shows the CLI calling all six readers with `&config.contract.seedelf_policy_id` (a `&String`). orders.rs:68 has `SundaeSwapV4,`, added in 183878f8 after 0.7.0. launch.rs:122 has `pub cant_come_back: Option<CantPayBack>,` on `pub struct Launch`, which has no private field. seedelf-core/README.md:5 says: "published so that `cargo install seedelf-cli` resolves ... expect breaking changes on a minor bump". Root CLAUDE.md:98 says: "on `0.x` Cargo reads a minor bump as breaking, which is the right regime for it". The project's own history fits that rule: comparing signatures between the tags, 0.6.0→0.6.1 changed none of core's, and 0.6.1→0.7.0 changed the lovejoin builders (`rewards: &mut Rewards`) and was a minor bump.
findings.fix: Make it 0.8.0: `[workspace.package]` and the four `[workspace.dependencies]` lines, then `cargo update --workspace` (Cargo.lock's six members), aiken.toml, RELEASE.md's two `version=` examples, and CLAUDE.md's "(0.8.0 today)". Reword bd45ee21's message to match. While there, mark `address::is_not_a_script` `#[deprecated(note = "counts the stake part: use is_key_address / is_script_address")]`, as seedelf-display did for `all_seedelfs` and `webserver_address`. 0.7.1 can't honestly be made compatible: deprecated wrappers could restore the six readers, but the new Protocol variant and the new Launch field would still break exhaustive matches and struct literals.
findings.owner_question: You asked for "a patch release". The changes since 0.7.0 break core's API (six utxos readers, a new orders::Protocol variant, a new field on Launch). Can this release be numbered 0.8.0, as CLAUDE.md's 0.x rule and core's README say? Or do you want 0.7.1, accepting that `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` stops building?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds. I reproduced it on HEAD (75956e22) without network access. Nothing in the tree guards against it.

**The requirement is a caret.** crates.io's index cache on this machine (~/.cargo/registry/index/index.crates.io-*/.cache/se/ed/seedelf-cli, read offline) records seedelf-cli 0.7.0 requiring `seedelf-core ^0.7.0`, `seedelf-crypto ^0.7.0`, `seedelf-display ^0.7.0` and `seedelf-koios ^0.7.0`. The cached seedelf-{core,crypto,koios,display}-0.7.0 sources are byte-identical to tag 0.7.0. HEAD sets every crate to "0.7.1" (seedelf-platform/Cargo.toml:14-17 and :28, from bd45ee21). So `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` without `--locked` would build the 0.7.0 CLI against 0.7.1.

**The API breaks.**
- The six readers take `contract: &Contract` where 0.7.0 took `seedelf_policy_id: &str`. On HEAD: utxos.rs:53, :81, :116, :147, :563, :613. At the tag: utxos.rs:32, :55, :85, :111, :436, :463. The change is 03cf290e, whose own message says "breaking for the published crate (0.x)".
- orders.rs:68 adds `SundaeSwapV4,` (183878f8, not in 0.7.0). Core has no `#[non_exhaustive]` anywhere.
- launch.rs:109-123: `pub struct Launch` has only public fields and gains `pub cant_come_back: Option<CantPayBack>` (26f6938e). It's re-exported at lovejoin/mod.rs:90.
- I diffed the public signatures of all four library crates between the tags. 0.7.0 to HEAD gives exactly this set, plus additions. koios and crypto changed no signature. display only deprecated `all_seedelfs` and `webserver_address`, so they still compile with warnings.
- The project's own history follows the rule: 0.6.0 to 0.6.1 changed no public item (a patch), and 0.6.1 to 0.7.0 added the `rewards: &mut Rewards` parameters and `Version::V2` (a minor bump).

**Behaviour changes that compile silently.**
- build.rs:3432-3434: `is_payable_address` no longer checks `is_not_a_script` (it did at 0.7.0's build.rs:3280-3284).
- launch.rs:207-213: `check_usable` now maps `Unusable::CantComeBack` to `Ok(Some(..))`, where 0.7.0 refused. All three builders take that path: `launch` (:337), `launch_apart` (:435) and `launch_from_account` (:684).

**The project's own rule says minor.** CLAUDE.md:98: "on `0.x` Cargo reads a minor bump as breaking, which is the right regime for it". seedelf-core/README.md:5, and the same line in the crypto, display and koios READMEs: "published so that `cargo install seedelf-cli` resolves ... expect breaking changes on a minor bump".

**Guards I looked for and didn't find.**
- Only `--locked` uses the packaged lock. README.md:12 and seedelf-platform/README.md:31 document `cargo install seedelf-cli` without it.
- No OWNER line names a number. DECISIONS.md says only "a CLI patch release" (:16, :61, in recommendations the owner approved), and :719 says "Core is a published crate, so it needs a version bump either way". So 0.7.1 isn't a decided exception. The number does what was decided, and the old CLI breaks because of it.

**One more scenario.** RELEASE.md:85-93 publishes core before the CLI. Between the two, crates.io's newest CLI is still 0.7.0, so the README's own `cargo install seedelf-cli` fails the same way until `cargo publish -p seedelf-cli` lands, and that command builds the CLI before it uploads. If that publish fails, the README's install stays broken. With 0.8.0 there's no such window.

**What else holds.** seedelf-data doesn't depend on these crates. bd45ee21 isn't on any remote-tracking branch, so its message can still be reworded.

**Severity.** Medium under "a claim wider than the code". 0.7.1 is a published compatibility claim that the code contradicts, it makes CLAUDE.md:98 and the READMEs' line false, and it can't be withdrawn once published. The harm is a failed build: no funds, and nothing gets stuck, since `--locked` or 0.7.1 still installs.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. **Workspace manifest.** seedelf-platform/Cargo.toml:14-17 and :28: change "0.7.1" to "0.8.0".
2. **Cargo.lock.** Change only the six member entries' `version = "0.7.1"` to "0.8.0": seedelf-cli, -core, -crypto, -display, -koios and -wasm. That's 12 lines, the same as bd45ee21. Check with `cargo tree --locked --offline -p seedelf-cli`; I did this in the copy and it passes.
   - Don't use `cargo update --workspace --offline`. Here it also moved dirs-sys's and rustix's `windows-sys` from 0.59.0 to 0.61.2, against the commit's "Nothing else in Cargo.lock changes".
   - RELEASE.md's online `cargo update --workspace` is fine where the network is allowed. Either way, `git diff --stat seedelf-platform/Cargo.lock` should show 12 lines.
3. **The other version lines.** seedelf-contracts/aiken.toml:2, RELEASE.md:59 and :106, and CLAUDE.md:98's "(0.8.0 today)".
4. **bd45ee21's message.** It's unpushed, so reword it, or follow it with a commit that says this.
   - Subject: "... to 0.8.0".
   - "For the CLI patch release" becomes "For the CLI release".
   - The reason: seedelf-core's API breaks since 0.7.0. The six utxos readers take `&Contract`, `orders::Protocol` gains `SundaeSwapV4`, and `lovejoin::Launch` gains `cant_come_back`. On top of that, `is_payable_address` now takes script addresses, and the launch builders no longer refuse a pool whose boxes can't come back. On 0.x that's a minor bump (CLAUDE.md:98 and the crates' READMEs).
5. **Archived records.** Leave "a CLI patch release" where it stands in review-51.md (:3, :7, :150, :160) and chunk-51-whole-review.md (:231, :260), since records aren't rewritten. Say in the PR text that the CLI release is 0.8.0, and why.
6. **Optional deprecation.** Mark `#[deprecated(note = "counts the stake part: use is_key_address / is_script_address")]` on address.rs:68 `is_not_a_script`. seedelf-core/tests/address_test.rs:46-74 still calls it, so those tests then need `#[allow(deprecated)]`, or `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` fails.
7. **No 0.7.1 compatibility shim.** Wrappers could restore the six readers. But adding `#[non_exhaustive]` to `Protocol`, or a private field to `Launch`, is itself breaking, and moving `cant_come_back` off `Launch` changes the builders' return types.
8. **Owner question.** Ask it as the finding words it, adding that under 0.7.1 the README's own `cargo install seedelf-cli` also fails during the publish, between RELEASE.md:91 and :93.
verdicts.test:
The check: does the published seedelf-cli 0.7.0 still build once this workspace's crates are on crates.io? I wrote it as a shell check in a copy of seedelf-platform. `<copy>` below stands for the scratchpad path calls/review/cli_1.

**Setup, in the copy:**
1. Replace seedelf-cli/ with `git archive 0.7.0 seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli`.
2. In its Cargo.toml, set `version = "0.7.0"` and turn the four `seedelf-* = { workspace = true }` into `seedelf-* = "0.7.0"`, which is the index's `^0.7.0`.
3. The workspace's `[patch.crates-io]` stands in for the publish. It serves the tree's crates wherever their version meets a requirement, and crates.io's own cached 0.7.0 otherwise.

**The script, `<copy>/published_cli_0_7_0.sh`:**
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# chunk 51, cli#1: does the published seedelf-cli 0.7.0 still build once this
# workspace's crates are on crates.io? (index: seedelf-* "^0.7.0"; cargo install
# without --locked takes the newest version each requirement admits)
cd "$(dirname "$0")/seedelf-platform" || exit 2
echo "workspace version: $(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)"
echo "what the 0.7.0 CLI resolves:"
cargo tree --offline -p seedelf-cli --depth 1 -e normal 2>&1 | grep -E "seedelf-(cli|core|crypto|koios|display)"
cargo check --offline -j 4 -p seedelf-cli --bins --message-format short 2>&1 |
  grep -E "^seedelf-cli/src/.*error|^error|could not compile|Finished"
status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "PASS: the published 0.7.0 CLI builds"; else echo "FAIL: cargo check exited $status"; fi
exit "$status"
```

verdicts.evidence:
The facts hold. The impact is lower than medium: the only outcome anyone can reach is a compile error, which fails safe and has a one-flag workaround. No funds are at risk.

Checked, and true:
1. The bump. bd45ee21 sets seedelf-platform/Cargo.toml:14-17 to `seedelf-core = "0.7.1"` (and crypto, display, koios) and :28 to `version = "0.7.1"`.
2. The six readers broke. At tag 0.7.0, and in the published crate (~/.cargo/registry/.../seedelf-core-0.7.0, whose every .rs equals the tag's), the six readers took `seedelf_policy_id: &str`. At HEAD they take `contract: &Contract`: utxos.rs:53 collect_all_wallet_utxos, :81 find_seedelf_datum, :116 find_seedelf_utxo, :147 collect_wallet_utxos, :563 find_all_seedelfs, :613 count_lovelace_and_utxos. 03cf290e's message says "breaking for the published crate (0.x)". The same change (343fb772) is on cli/stranger-rows, so any CLI release carries it.
3. CLI 0.7.0's calls no longer compile. It passes a `&String` (constants.rs:11, `pub seedelf_policy_id: String`): `utxos::collect_all_wallet_utxos(scalar, &config.contract.seedelf_policy_id, every_utxo)?` at balance.rs:37. The same holds at sweep.rs:151, transfer.rs:102/112 (`let policy_id: &str = &chain.config.contract.seedelf_policy_id`), fund.rs:103, remove.rs:55, util/find.rs:37, util/mint.rs:68 and util/statistics.rs:16. Each is E0308.
4. Cargo would pick core 0.7.1 for CLI 0.7.0.
   - At 0.7.0 the CLI declares `seedelf-core = { workspace = true }`, and the workspace says "0.7.0". Published, that becomes `version = "0.7.0"`, a caret requirement, as the published core 0.7.0 shows for its own deps (`[dependencies.seedelf-crypto] version = "0.7.0"`).
   - `[patch.crates-io]` doesn't travel with a published crate, and no crate declares a rust-version.
   - cargo 1.98.1's cargo-install.1:91 says "By default, the Cargo.lock file that is included with the package will be ignored". Lines :118-121 say `--version 0.7.0` installs exactly that version.
5. The other public breaks.
   - orders.rs:61-73 `pub enum Protocol` gained `SundaeSwapV4,` (:68) with no #[non_exhaustive] (183878f8, after the 0.7.0 tag).
   - launch.rs:109-123 `pub struct Launch`, every field pub and re-exported at lovejoin/mod.rs:90, gained `pub cant_come_back: Option<CantPayBack>` (:122). Neither can be made 0.7-compatible.
6. Silent changes.
   - build.rs:3432 `is_payable_address` lost `&& is_not_a_script(..)`.
   - check_usable now returns `Ok(Some(CantPayBack{..}))` where 0.7.0 bailed.
   - note.rs:27 `MAX_NOTE_CHARS` went from 64 to 500, which the finding didn't list.
7. History fits the rule. Diffing the published crates, core 0.6.0 to 0.6.1 changed no public signature, struct or enum. 0.6.1 to 0.7.0 changed 13 (`rewards: &mut Rewards`) and was a minor bump. CLAUDE.md:98 and seedelf-core/README.md:5 ("expect breaking changes on a minor bump") state the regime.
8. Nothing later catches it. No workflow runs a semver check, and RELEASE.md:78-94 runs only fmt, clippy, test and publish. crates.io never overwrites a version.

Impact:
- Who reaches it: a user running `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` without --locked once core 0.7.1 is out, from a pinned script, CI or a bounty reproducer working against 0.7.0. Also any `cargo install seedelf-cli` in the few minutes between RELEASE.md's `cargo publish -p seedelf-core` and `-p seedelf-cli`, while 0.7.0 is still the newest CLI.
- What they lose: a build, no money. `--locked`, or installing 0.7.1, fixes it.
- What's unaffected: the documented `cargo install seedelf-cli` (it picks CLI 0.7.1), the signed binaries, and seedelf-display/koios/crypto, whose changes are additive only (signing_page_address, script_transactions, SubmitError).
- The compile error is protective. CLI 0.7.0 guards sweep.rs:139 and remove.rs:45 with `build::is_payable_address`. If it linked against core 0.7.1, it would pay a script address, the Seedelf contract's own included, with no warning.
- Third-party crates on seedelf-core 0.7: none known. Core's README calls it internal, and I couldn't check reverse deps offline.

Medium's only hook here is "a claim wider than the code" (the version number and README:5's implied promise). What that claim costs is a loud build failure in an edge case, so it grades low. It's still worth fixing before the tag: it's cheap now and permanent after publish. The number isn't fixed in DECISIONS ("CLI patch release"; g1b: "needs a version bump either way"), so the finding's owner question stands.

findings.title: sweep --ada-handle still refuses a handle held at the Seedelf contract, while sweep -a and the web wallet pay that address with the warning
findings.scenario: A friend keeps `$friend` in their Seedelf balance, so the handle's UTxO sits at the contract's enterprise address `addr1w<wallet hash>`. `seedelf-cli sweep --ada-handle friend -l 5000000` stops with "ADA Handle Is In Wallet Address". `seedelf-cli sweep -a addr1w<wallet hash> -l 5000000` prints the script warning and pays it. Seedelf Wallet's Make public or Send to `$friend` also resolves it, sets `script: true` and pays with send.warn.script. So three copies of one payee rule now give two answers. The CLI's check is also only a string comparison with the enterprise form: a handle at the contract's staked form passes it and is paid with the warning. B16 (2) asks for a warning, not a refusal, for script payment parts, and the ledger refuses neither.
findings.evidence: koios.rs:751-755: `return if payment_address == wallet_addr { Err("ADA Handle Is In Wallet Address".to_string()) } else { Ok(payment_address.to_string()) };`. sweep.rs:96-99 passes `address::wallet_contract(network_flag, ...)` (the enterprise form) as `wallet_addr`, then sweep.rs:140-143 runs `build::is_payable_address` and `super::warn_if_a_script(&addr)`. destination.ts:55-76 runs `checkPayable` and then `...(isScriptAddress(address) ? { script: true } : {})`, with no contract exception. G1b's notes name this sibling as left alone because no group owns seedelf-koios.
findings.fix: In `ada_handle_address`, return the holder's address for a handle at the contract too (drop the `wallet_addr` refusal; the parameter can stay for compatibility), and let sweep.rs's `warn_if_a_script` say it, as for `-a`. Add a CLI test like `sweep_pays_a_scripts_address_and_says_it_carries_no_datum` that goes through `--ada-handle`. If you keep the refusal on purpose, the README's Addresses bullet should say a handle held at the Seedelf contract is refused.
findings.owner_question: Should `sweep --ada-handle` keep refusing a handle held at the Seedelf contract (a no-datum payment there is anyone's to take), or warn and pay it, as `sweep -a` and the web wallet now do?

verdicts.evidence:
I traced this on HEAD 75956e22 and found no guard the finder missed. The new test reproduces it.

Where the value starts and where it goes wrong:
- seedelf-cli/src/commands/sweep.rs:96-99 builds `wallet_addr` from `address::wallet_contract(network_flag, ...)`. That is the enterprise form only: address.rs:96-108 uses `ShelleyDelegationPart::Null`, so the address is addr1w… (addr_test1w… on preprod).
- sweep.rs:100-112 passes it to `ada_handle_address` and turns any Err into `bail!(err)`.
- seedelf-koios/src/koios.rs:751-755 compares bech32 strings: `return if payment_address == wallet_addr { Err("ADA Handle Is In Wallet Address".to_string()) } else { Ok(payment_address.to_string()) };`. So a handle held at the contract's enterprise address stops the sweep before anything is built. A handle at the contract's staked form (addr1z…) is a different string, so it gets through.
- sweep.rs:140-143 then runs `build::is_payable_address`. After 63cd92fb that is any Shelley address on the network (build.rs:3432-3434). Then `super::warn_if_a_script(&addr)` (commands/mod.rs:21-30) prints the warning. Core's builders (build.rs:3474 address_payment, :3696 sweep_all) refuse only through the same check_payable, and nothing in them is specific to the contract.

The round made this split:
- At 984ff48f, `is_payable_address` refused every address with a script part (`is_not_a_script`). All three paths refused then: `-a` the contract, a handle at the enterprise form, a handle at the staked form.
- 63cd92fb widened the predicate and left koios.rs untouched. The round touched seedelf-koios in no commit (git log 984ff48f..HEAD).
- G1b's own notes in round1.json name this sibling as not fixed: "koios.rs:751 `ada_handle_address`: the CLI refuses a handle held at the Seedelf contract's address ... a refusal the ledger doesn't make. No group owns seedelf-koios." The same notes tell the owner that Send, Make public, sweep and remove "now pay the Seedelf contract's own address too".

The web wallet goes the other way:
- destination.ts:56-67 resolves `$handle` through assetNftAddress, and koios.ts:1153-1157 has no contract check.
- :68 runs checkPayable, which passes now, and :75 sets `script: true`.
- CardanoSend.tsx:330 and Withdraw.tsx:333 show ScriptNote, which is send.warn.script.
- script-address.test.ts:257-259 already pins paying the contract's address.

The rule this breaks: DECISIONS B16 (2) says script payment parts get "a short .warn. line instead of the refusal", and G1b's scope lists the CLI's sweep.rs. The ledger takes such a payment.

Docs:
- README.md:153's new Addresses bullet ("`sweep` and `remove` pay any address on the network but a stake address. A script's address (a multisig's, a contract's) they pay too") is false for `--ada-handle`.
- README.md:123 ("`sweep` pays a key address or an ADA Handle's address") was not updated for r2a#1.

What does hold: the refusal loses no money. wallet.ak at 5b82530 has `None -> True`, so a payment there is anyone's to take, and the refusal is the protective outcome. The user can still pay with `-a`. That is why this is low (an edge case where an action is refused for no ledger reason, no loss), and the keep-or-drop choice is the owner's question.

The test run on a copy of HEAD shows all three answers:
- `-a` the contract: sent with the warning, 2 ADA with no datum.
- A handle at the staked form: sent with the warning.
- A handle at the enterprise form: "ADA Handle Is In Wallet Address", nothing paid, no warning.
verdicts.fix_notes:
This follows B16 (2) and the no-paternalistic-guards rule:

1. In seedelf-platform/seedelf-koios/src/koios.rs:751-755, replace the comparison with `return Ok(payment_address.to_string());`.
2. Keep the parameter but rename it `_wallet_addr` (koios.rs:707). seedelf-koios is published, and dropping the parameter changes the signature, which on 0.x needs a minor bump rather than the 0.7.1 patch. If it is dropped anyway, also update sweep.rs:96-99/:105 and tests/koios_test.rs:24-28.
3. Nothing else changes. sweep.rs:143 `warn_if_a_script` already warns for both forms of the contract's address, as it does for `-a`.

I checked this in a copy: with exactly that change, the new test passes, and `cargo test -p seedelf-cli -p seedelf-koios` stays green (the cli suite's 80 integration tests and every other offline test). No offline test pins the refusal. koios_test.rs `find_ada_handle` is live-only and expects a key address, so it is unaffected.

Add the test below to seedelf-cli/tests/cli: either as its own module registered in main.rs, or folded into sweep.rs next to `sweep_pays_a_scripts_address_and_says_it_carries_no_datum`. It mounts GET /api/v1/asset_nft_address on the harness's mock.

If the owner keeps the refusal on purpose:
- Compare the payment credential instead of the string, so the staked form addr1z… is refused too. Today it is paid. For example, parse with `Address::from_bech32` and refuse `Address::Shelley(s)` when `s.payment()` is `ShelleyPaymentPart::Script(h)` with `h == wallet_contract_hash`.
- Better still, do that check in sweep.rs on the resolved Address, so koios.rs needs no contract knowledge.
- Make the message say why: a payment there has no datum and anyone can take it.
- Add a clause to README.md:153's Addresses bullet saying `sweep --ada-handle` refuses a handle held at the Seedelf contract.

Either way, in the same edit change README.md:123 "`sweep` pays a key address or an ADA Handle's address" to "an address". r2a#1 made sweep pay a script's address too.

Line 153's "any address on the network but a stake address" also leaves out Byron, which `is_payable_address` refuses. findings.title: Core's public docs still say "key address" where script addresses are now paid
findings.scenario: A crate user reading the docs.rs pages for 0.7.1 sees `Payee::Address` documented as "A key address", `ScriptSpend::change_to` as "to `addr`, a key address", `AddressPayment` as "A payment to a key address", and `sweep_most` as "`to`, a key address". `address_minimum_lovelace_with_assets` is documented as "for a non-script address output". Since r2a#1, all of them take a script's address: `check_payable` accepts one, the CLI's `remove` and `sweep --all` pay it through `change_to`, and sweep.rs:130 prices it through `address_minimum_lovelace_with_assets`. G1b updated `RestTo::Address` and `account_send(_many)` but not these.
findings.evidence: build.rs:673 `/// A key address. Tokens go MAXIMUM_TOKENS_PER_UTXO to an output.` and :1719-1720 `/// Sends what's left ... to addr, a key /// address, instead of back into the contract`. :3548 `/// A payment to a key address from the Seedelf balance.` and :3629 `/// [transfer_most] to to, a key address`. transaction.rs:240 `/// Minimum lovelace for a non-script address output with assets.` CLAUDE.md:58 "`change_to(addr)` sends the change to a key address instead of the contract".
findings.fix: Say "an address on this network ([`is_payable_address`])" in the four build.rs docs. Say "for an output at `address` with assets and no datum" in transaction.rs:240. In platform CLAUDE.md:58, say "sends the change to an address instead of the contract".

checked_ok: r2a#1 in core: `is_payable_address` is Shelley plus the right network (build.rs:3432). `is_key_address` and `is_script_address` read the payment part alone (address.rs:76, :86), and payable_address_test.rs pins all eight CIP-19 shapes, with stake, Byron and other-network addresses refused. `is_not_a_script` is kept, its doc pointing to the new pair.

create, fund and util extract check `is_key_address && is_on_correct_network`, so a type-2 payer (key payment part, script stake part) passes. That's sound for the ledger: the payment key signs, and a collateral input needs only a key payment credential. Script payers stay refused, since the CLI can't witness them and collateral must be key-locked.

sweep and remove: `is_payable_address`, then `warn_if_a_script`, before the password prompt (which doesn't clear the screen). The order holds for -a, a resolved --ada-handle, --all and --utxo. The English line is identical to en.json's send.warn.script. Core's sweep, sweep_all and sweep_from check again through check_address. remove's `change_to` is unchecked in core but the CLI checks first. No other CLI command pays an arbitrary address.

r2a#3 in the CLI's blind path: the sort key is (last, holds_tokens, Reverse(lovelace)) and the last prefix is the same full set as before, so nothing the old order paid is refused. A pile that adds less than nothing can't make a short set pay on its own. `adds` prices against minimum_deposit, which is right for all three CLI blind-path spends (transfer, sweep with an amount, util mint), since their change goes back to the contract. rows.rs's window ranks by the same rule (`worth` with minimum_deposit), so the two copies agree.

Core's public signatures for mint_apart, transfer_apart and sweep_many_apart are unchanged. select_script_inputs is pub(crate), and its one outside caller, launch_apart, passes &chain.params. build.rs holds every edit G1a, G1b and G4a2 listed: the import drop, is_payable_address, check_payable's words, the RestTo and account_send docs, adds, less_than_nothing, apart's `last` in steps 1 to 3 and orders a to d, one_more's generic rank, Purpose::Mint's ranks. I found no lost or overwritten hunk.
B10: sweep --all and external sweep are untouched (Max spends every UTxO), and the README line is in Limits as decided. Its 1.5 ADA a 20 matches the re-check's 14.5 ₳ for 200 tokens.

r4#8: util mint -g -p re-randomizes after is_valid (mint.rs:90). An identity register is still refused by mint_from's is_payable. The README row says so, and the test asserts that the two mints' datums differ, neither uses G1 as its generator, and both are the recipient's.
gap-g8#3: the CLI never builds a Note. Core's split keeps lines to 64 bytes, and 500 matches activity.ts's and CardanoSend.tsx's NOTE_MAX.

findings.title: The policy now promises Translate never gets the recovery phrase, but the phrase's words still show as unmarked page text while it's typed
findings.scenario: A user whose Chrome is in German has Translate on for the wallet's page (offered, or Always translate English). They restore by typing their 24 words in Restore. The same happens in Settings → Check recovery phrase and in Create's three confirm words. For each word, PhraseInput shows up to 5 BIP39 words that start with what's typed, as ordinary page text with no translate attribute. After 3-4 letters the list is down to the word itself. Chrome keeps translating text a translated page adds later, so those words go to Google. The policy, newly, says the opposite: the 18 November entry has 'Chrome's Translate no longer gets your recovery phrase … neither sends them to Google nor changes them', and the Translate line has 'but not your recovery phrase'. Its row 13 says the phrase 'is never sent anywhere', and privacy.md says the 24 words are kept out. Only the shown grid is marked.
findings.who: user (their own Translate setting); Google receives the phrase's words

findings.title: 0.7.1 is a patch bump over a seedelf-core public API that has broken since 0.7.0
findings.scenario: Once seedelf-core 0.7.1 is on crates.io, `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` (no --locked, cargo install's default) resolves seedelf-core ^0.7.0 to 0.7.1 and fails to compile. Tag 0.7.0's balance.rs:37 calls `utxos::collect_all_wallet_utxos(scalar, &config.contract.seedelf_policy_id, every_utxo)`, and the function now takes `contract: &Contract`. find_seedelf_datum, find_seedelf_utxo and collect_wallet_utxos changed the same way (x2#2). Launch and AccountLaunch, all-pub structs, gained a pub field (launch.rs:122, :465), which breaks any struct literal. Any other crate on seedelf-core 0.7 breaks at its next `cargo update`. bd45ee21's own message says the round changes 'seedelf-core's public API, a published crate'. A published version can't be taken back, only yanked.
findings.who: nobody (the release itself); it hits anyone who builds an older CLI, or a crate on core 0.7, from crates.io
findings.evidence: utxos.rs:53-56 `pub fn collect_all_wallet_utxos(sk: Scalar, contract: &Contract, utxos: Vec<UtxoResponse>)`; `git show 0.7.0:seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli/src/commands/balance.rs`:37 passes `&config.contract.seedelf_policy_id`; Cargo.toml:14 `seedelf-core = "0.7.1"`, :28 `version = "0.7.1"`; seedelf-core/README.md:5 'Its API is on the 0.x line and still moving, so expect breaking changes on a minor bump'; CLAUDE.md:98 'on 0.x Cargo reads a minor bump as breaking, which is the right regime for it'.
findings.fix: Make it 0.8.0 in each place bd45ee21 touched: [workspace.package] and the four [workspace.dependencies] in Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock's six members, aiken.toml, RELEASE.md:59 and :106, and CLAUDE.md:98. That's the regime the crates' READMEs and CLAUDE.md state. If the owner keeps 0.7.1, record that 0.7.0 then builds only with --locked.
findings.owner_question: 0.8.0 for this CLI release, the documented bump for an API change, or 0.7.1 knowing that `cargo install seedelf-cli@0.7.0` stops building without --locked?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 69d001e8. Two corrections, one break it missed, and I'd rate it low, not medium.

What I checked, and it holds:
- bd45ee21 sets 0.7.1 in every place the finding lists. Cargo.toml:14-17 has `seedelf-core = "0.7.1"` and its three siblings, and :28 `version = "0.7.1"`. Also aiken.toml:2, RELEASE.md:59 and :106, CLAUDE.md:98, and Cargo.lock's six members.
- Its own message says the round changes "seedelf-core's public API, a published crate".
- RELEASE.md:85-93 publishes all five crates, core included.
- The published seedelf-cli 0.7.0 asks for core with a caret, so `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` will take core 0.7.1. Tag 0.7.0's Cargo.toml:14 has `seedelf-core = "0.7.0"` and the CLI uses `{ workspace = true }`, so the published manifest says `version = "0.7.0"`, meaning ^0.7.0.
  - The registry copy of seedelf-core 0.7.0 is identical to tag 0.7.0 (`diff -r` of src/ is clean). Its manifest shows the same rewrite: `[dependencies.seedelf-crypto] version = "0.7.0"`.
  - `cargo install` ignores the packaged Cargo.lock unless `--locked` is given.
  - No crate manifest changed between 0.7.0 and HEAD. Cargo.lock differs only in the six versions.
- The API break is real, in utxos.rs. At 0.7.0 these took `seedelf_policy_id: &str`, and now they take `contract: &Contract`:
  - `collect_all_wallet_utxos` (:53-56), `find_seedelf_datum` (:81), `find_seedelf_utxo` (:116) and `collect_wallet_utxos` (:147), as cited.
  - Also `find_all_seedelfs` (:563) and `count_lovelace_and_utxos` (:613), which the finding missed.
  - Tag 0.7.0's balance.rs:37 passes `&config.contract.seedelf_policy_id`. Reproduced: tag 0.7.0's CLI, with its published requirements, resolves to HEAD's core v0.7.1 and fails with 9 E0308 errors (see test).
- DECISIONS has no OWNER line that picks the number. "CLI patch release" appears only in recommendation text (DECISIONS.md:16, :61, :617, :719, :851) and in BRIEF.md:3 ("a patch release"). :719 says only "Core is a published crate, so it needs a version bump either way". bd45ee21 credits the owner with the order ("the CLI first, then the wallet"), not the number. So this isn't a decided behaviour, and the owner question stands.
- The documented rule says this is a minor bump. CLAUDE.md:98: "on `0.x` Cargo reads a minor bump as breaking, which is the right regime for it". README.md:5 of core, crypto, koios and display: "expect breaking changes on a minor bump".

Corrections:
1. AccountLaunch is not all-pub. `chain`, `inputs`, `collateral`, `outputs`, `policy`, `one_shot`, `staking`, `change_addr` and `invalid_hereafter` are private (lovejoin/launch.rs:448-458). So its new `pub cant_come_back` (:465) breaks nothing: the probe's `AccountLaunch { seed: _, …, .. }` compiles at HEAD.
   - Launch is all-pub (:109-123, re-exported at lovejoin/mod.rs:90-93). Its new field at :122 (26f6938e, this round) breaks struct literals and exhaustive patterns. The probe gets E0027 at HEAD and compiles at 0.7.0.
2. The utxos break predates the round. It came in 03cf290e, x2#2's fix, before 984ff48f. bd45ee21 only picks the number.

Missed break: `orders::Protocol` (orders.rs:61-73) is a pub enum without `#[non_exhaustive]`. It gained `SundaeSwapV4` (183878f8, chunk 47, already on main), which breaks any exhaustive match. Two more changes still compile but behave differently:
- `is_payable_address` (build.rs:3432) now accepts script addresses.
- `MAX_NOTE_CHARS` went from 64 to 500 (note.rs).

Scope: crypto, koios and display only add items (koios `SubmitError` and `script_transactions`, display `signing_page_address` plus deprecations). So the published core 0.7.0, which asks for crypto ^0.7.0 and koios ^0.7.0, still builds against their 0.7.1. The break is core's alone.

Why low: no funds or privacy are at stake, and the failure is a loud compile error. It hits only `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` without `--locked`, or a crate that depends on core ^0.7. The README calls core internal, and seedelf-wasm has `publish = false`. `cargo install seedelf-cli`, the documented command (README.md:12, seedelf-platform/README.md:31), gets 0.7.1 with core 0.7.1 and works. Yanking core 0.7.1 would undo it. It is still cheap to fix before anything is published, and the release contradicts the stated rule.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. Make it 0.8.0 using RELEASE.md's own block with `version="0.8.0"`.
   - Its seds are anchored. They change only aiken.toml's first `version =`, Cargo.toml's first `version =` (:28) and the four `^seedelf-* =` lines (:14-17).
   - Then run `cargo update --workspace --manifest-path seedelf-platform/Cargo.toml`. It moves only Cargo.lock's six members (:2413, :2451, :2479, :2503, :2517, :2530).
   - Then edit RELEASE.md:59 and :106 to `version="0.8.0"`, and CLAUDE.md:98 to "(0.8.0 today)".
2. Never blanket-replace "0.7.1". `blstrs = "0.7.1"` is a third-party dependency in seedelf-cli/Cargo.toml:16, seedelf-core:13, seedelf-crypto:14, seedelf-display:11 and seedelf-web-wallet/wasm:16. Cargo.lock:290 and :2607 are also third-party 0.7.1 entries.
3. Reword bd45ee21's message, or the follow-up commit's, to say it's a minor bump because core's public API broke. List the breaks:
   - the six utxos functions that now take `&Contract`;
   - `Launch.cant_come_back`;
   - `orders::Protocol::SundaeSwapV4`;
   - the wider `is_payable_address`.
4. Drop the finding's AccountLaunch claim; that change is compatible.
5. No code change is needed. The 0.8.0 CLI resolves core ^0.8, and an installed 0.7.0 resolves core ^0.7, which then stays at 0.7.0. The wallet's 1.x line is unaffected.
6. If the owner keeps 0.7.1, the CLI release body and RELEASE.md should say:
   - seedelf-cli 0.7.0 then installs only with `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0 --locked`;
   - a crate on core 0.7 must pin `=0.7.0`.
   If 0.7.1 goes out by mistake, `cargo yank --version 0.7.1 seedelf-core` brings back 0.7.0's fresh resolution, and the release can be republished as 0.8.0.

Reproduces the finding's scenario offline in a copy of HEAD's seedelf-platform (rsync as instructed, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$HOME/.cache/seedelf-calls/review-target-docs_2). It ran under `nice -n 10 systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=0 timeout 30m bash ./docs_2_test.sh`. TEST resolves HEAD's crates through the workspace's [patch.crates-io], which cargo uses only because 0.7.1 matches ^0.7.0, the way a registry 0.7.1 would be taken. The copy, its target, the control copy and the script were deleted afterwards.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# TEST    = tag 0.7.0's seedelf-cli, its published requirements, HEAD's crates (0.7.1)
# CONTROL = tag 0.7.0's seedelf-cli, its published requirements, tag 0.7.0's crates
set -u
REPO=.
R=<scratchpad>/calls/review/docs_2
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$HOME/.cache/seedelf-calls/review-target-docs_2
published_cli() { # the manifest cargo publish writes: version and seedelf-* = "0.7.0" (caret)
  rm -rf "$1/seedelf-cli"
  git -C "$REPO" archive 0.7.0 seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli | tar -x -C "$1" --strip-components=1
  sed -i -e 's/^version\.workspace = true$/version = "0.7.0"/' \
         -e 's/^\(seedelf-[a-z]*\) = { workspace = true }$/\1 = "0.7.0"/' "$1/seedelf-cli/Cargo.toml"
}
published_cli "$R/seedelf-platform"
mkdir -p "$R/control"; git -C "$REPO" archive 0.7.0 seedelf-platform | tar -x -C "$R/control"
published_cli "$R/control/seedelf-platform"
run() {
  echo "=== $1"
  ( cd "$2" && cargo tree --offline -p seedelf-cli --depth 1 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'seedelf-' )
  ( cd "$2" && cargo check --offline -p seedelf-cli --bins --lib -j 6 --message-format short > "$R/$1.log" 2>&1 )
  local rc=$?; grep -v -E '^\s+(Compiling|Checking|Locking|Updating)\b' "$R/$1.log"; echo "=== $1: cargo exit $rc"
}
run CONTROL "$R/control/seedelf-platform"
run TEST "$R/seedelf-platform"
```

Output:

```
=== probe on head
seedelf-core/examples/launch_probe.rs:6:9: error[E0027]: pattern does not mention field `cant_come_back`: missing field `cant_come_back`
```

verdicts.evidence:
The main claim holds. Two corrections and one missed case follow. I checked everything by reading the code and git history. Nothing was built.

**Why `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` breaks once 0.7.1 is published**
- At tag 0.7.0, seedelf-platform/Cargo.toml:14 has `seedelf-core = "0.7.0"`, and seedelf-cli takes it with `{ workspace = true }`. The published requirement is therefore ^0.7.0, which means >=0.7.0 and <0.8.0.
- Without `--locked`, `cargo install` ignores the packaged Cargo.lock and resolves again, so it picks seedelf-core 0.7.1.
- HEAD's seedelf-core/src/utxos.rs:53-57 is `pub fn collect_all_wallet_utxos(sk: Scalar, contract: &Contract, utxos: Vec<UtxoResponse>)`.
- The same `seedelf_policy_id: &str` → `contract: &Contract` change is at :81 find_seedelf_datum, :116 find_seedelf_utxo, :147 collect_wallet_utxos, :563 find_all_seedelfs and :613 count_lovelace_and_utxos. A signature diff of every top-level pub fn between 0.7.0 and HEAD shows exactly these six changed and none removed.
- CLI 0.7.0 passes `&config.contract.seedelf_policy_id` (a `&String`) at nine sites: balance.rs:37, fund.rs:103, remove.rs:55, sweep.rs:151, transfer.rs:102 and :112, util/find.rs:37, util/mint.rs:68, util/statistics.rs:16. Each is an E0308 against core 0.7.1.
- bd45ee21 sets 0.7.1 (Cargo.toml:14-17 and :28).
- The documented rule says a breaking change needs a minor bump. All four crate READMEs say at :5: "published so that `cargo install seedelf-cli` resolves ... expect breaking changes on a minor bump". CLAUDE.md:98 says the same.
- Past releases followed that rule. 0.6.0 → 0.6.1 changed no library source, and the API changes shipped as 0.5.0, 0.6.0 and 0.7.0.
- Nothing catches it before publish. No workflow runs a semver check. release.yml:35 builds `--locked` against the workspace's path patches. RELEASE.md:85-93 publishes straight to crates.io.

**Correction 1: when the break happened**
- The break is 03cf290e. It is on cli/stranger-rows, which was merged at 984ff48f, before this round.
- Its own commit message says: "The six reader signatures in seedelf-core take the contract config in place of the policy id: breaking for the published crate (0.x); only the CLI calls them."
- This round's own public changes to core are additive, except that `Launch` gained `pub cant_come_back` (launch.rs:122).

**Correction 2: AccountLaunch**
- The finding says adding a field breaks AccountLaunch. That part is wrong.
- AccountLaunch (launch.rs:448-466) has nine private fields: chain, inputs, collateral, outputs, policy, one_shot, staking, change_addr and invalid_hereafter. No code outside the crate can write it as a struct literal, so a new pub field breaks nothing.
- `Launch` (launch.rs:109-123) has only pub fields, so adding a field is a break, but only in theory: CLI 0.7.0 never uses lovejoin::launch or orders.

**Another break since 0.7.0 (not in the finding)**
- orders.rs:61 `pub enum Protocol` is not marked non_exhaustive, and it gained `SundaeSwapV4` (183878f8). That breaks any outside exhaustive match. The CLI doesn't use it.

**Missed case: the publish window**
- RELEASE.md publishes core at :91 and the CLI at :93. Between core 0.7.1 and cli 0.7.1 reaching the index (cli's verify build takes minutes), the README's plain `cargo install seedelf-cli` (seedelf-platform/README.md:31) resolves cli 0.7.0 with core 0.7.1 and fails to compile.
- With 0.8.0 there's no such window, because cli 0.7.0 stays on core 0.7.0.

**Impact**
- Who it hits:
  - anyone who pins 0.7.0 from crates.io without `--locked`;
  - anyone who installs during that publish window;
  - any outside crate on core ^0.7 that calls the six readers. None are known, and the README calls core an internal crate.
- Who it doesn't hit:
  - the README's own path: `cargo install seedelf-cli`, which README.md:34 also says to rerun to update, gets 0.7.1 throughout, and it compiles;
  - signed binaries;
  - `--path` builds from a 0.7.0 checkout, which use path deps.
- What's lost is a compile error, with ready workarounds: `--locked`, installing 0.7.1, or the signed binary. No funds, no privacy and no stuck state are involved.
- It can be repaired after publishing (publish 0.8.0 and yank the 0.7.1 crates), but that's messy.
- That's a small cost in an edge case, so low rather than medium. It is free to fix now, before the tag.

findings.title: gap-g9#1's new session-storage record of who spent the wallet's UTxOs is in no policy entry
findings.scenario: On mainnet, while unlocked, readIndexView now keeps which transactions spent the wallet's own private UTxOs, the newest 100, gathered across reads. They sit in chrome.storage.session under seedelf.contract.mainnet, so a balance reading later still knows who made the change. G6a reported this as its own addition, a departure from the decision's 'no record' (its note 2), and handed it to G8. findings.evidence: contract-scan.ts:115 `const SPENT_BY_KEPT = 100;`, :126 `const newest = [...all].slice(-SPENT_BY_KEPT);`, :412 `const view: Kept = { owned, seedelfs, height: 0, fullAt: 0, ...withSpentBy((await session.get<Kept>(key))?.spentBy, spentBy) };`. round1.json G6a policy_facts[1]: 'this cache is my addition … The newest 100 are kept, in the existing seedelf.contract.<network> view'. On mainnet, while unlocked, the wallet keeps which transactions spent your private UTxOs, as our server reports to everyone, in memory-only session storage that's cleared at a lock. verdicts.evidence:
I traced it on HEAD 69d001e8. The cache is real, it is a new record, and no policy line names it. I found no guard the finder missed.

Where it starts:
- contract-scan.ts:356-365 (readIndexView) builds `spentBy` from the private index's `since` answer. It keys each spending transaction's hash (64-hex only, :363) to the wallet's own refs that the transaction spent (`ownRefs`, :358). That covers every spend of an own row, this device's own sends included, not only another profile's.
- :412 `const view: Kept = { owned, seedelfs, height: 0, fullAt: 0, ...withSpentBy((await session.get<Kept>(key))?.spentBy, spentBy) };`, then :413 `keep(session, key, view)`.
- The key is `seedelf.contract.<network>` (:131, :283), in `session` = chromeArea(chrome.storage.session) (sw.ts:148).
- withSpentBy (:119-127) merges the new spenders with the ones already kept, and :126 `const newest = [...all].slice(-SPENT_BY_KEPT);` keeps 100 spending transactions (:115).
- A Koios read carries them forward (:220 `...withSpentBy(kept?.spentBy, {})`), and so does forgetContractView (`...kept`).

Scope and lifetime:
- Mainnet only in production. privateIndexClient (private-index.ts:362-371) returns an index only where the data origin exists, Koios-only is off and the private part is up.
- A lock clears it: wallet.ts:733 `session.clear()` in wipe(), and lockKeeps carries only SESSION_SENDS and the refusals. My test checks this.
- It's used only on the device: balances.ts:304 and :435 hand `view.spentBy` to activity.arrived (activity.ts:533, :556). Nothing sends it anywhere.
- `git blame` puts :107-127 and :409-412 in d46533dd, G6a's commit.

It departs from the decision:
- DECISIONS, gap-g9#1: "The fix adds no request (the answer already has the spender) and no record", with policy entry False.
- round1.json G6a policy_facts[1] says it plainly: "for G8 to decide; the decision said no policy entry for gap-g9#1, and this cache is my addition … The newest 100 are kept, in the existing `seedelf.contract.<network>` view". G6a's note 2 calls it "A departure from the decision".
- No OWNER line accepts it.

Nothing names it:
- G8's seven policy_facts don't mention gap-g9#1.
- `git diff 984ff48f..HEAD` leaves policy row 16 unchanged.
- The 18 November entry (:93) has no such clause. A grep of privacy-policy.md finds no "profile" and no "which transactions spent".
- privacy.md:267 ("Which contract UTxOs are yours is kept in memory and in `chrome.storage.session`…") is silent too. privacy.md:177 describes the behaviour only, not that the spenders are kept.
- Only architecture.md:148 and :419 list it, as the finder said.

The rule is applied this way elsewhere:
- 12 October 2026 got a dated entry for keeping the IDs of collateral payments, newest 20, so Activity can name them.
- 5 October 2026 and the 18 November entry got lines for declined sites in session storage, and OWNER B7 asked for a policy line for that session-storage change this round.

What I checked that limits the harm:
- The data is session-only, gone at lock, and is the user's own spends as the server tells everyone.
- While unlocked, session storage already holds the entropy, and policy :87 says history is readable then.
- So nothing reaches anyone. It's only a missing disclosure the owner's rule requires, which is low.

Both fixes, tried in a copy:
- Policy clause added to row 16 and the 18 November entry: my test passes.
- Union dropped at :412 (`withSpentBy(undefined, spentBy)`): my test passes, but another-profile-spend.test.ts's fold test fails with "AssertionError: expected 'Received' to be 'Already in your private balance'". Dropping the cache brings gap-g9#1's harm back whenever another read folds the spend in before the balance reading.
verdicts.fix_notes:
This is the owner's call (keep or drop), but the two options don't cost the same. My recommendation is to keep the cache and add the words.

Keep (recommended):
- It's the more private behaviour, and it only holds what the server tells everyone, in session storage, until a lock.
- privacy-policy.md:93, after the gap-g1#2 sentence ("…a note whose transaction never lands goes after 30 days."), add: "On mainnet, while the wallet is unlocked, it now also keeps which transactions spent your private UTxOs, the newest 100, as our server reports them to everyone, in memory-only session storage that a lock clears: so what your recovery phrase sends from another browser profile or device reads as money already yours, never as a payment received."
- Row 16, after "otherwise it's kept in session storage and cleared when you lock.", add: "On mainnet, that session storage also keeps which transactions spent your private UTxOs, the newest 100, so what your recovery phrase sends from another browser profile or device isn't read as a payment received."
- Say "your private UTxOs", not "another profile's spends". The cache also records this device's own sends (`ownRefs` is every own row).
- privacy.md:267 (On this device): add "and, on mainnet, which transactions spent the wallet's own rows, as the private index names them, the newest 100 (`spentBy`), in the session copy only".
- The Effective date stays 18 November 2026. The policy is English only, so nothing needs back-translating.
- Don't commit a test that reads the .md files. G8's note 1 says that would put docs PRs on the 40-minute check. The code side is already pinned by another-profile-spend.test.ts's fold test.

Drop (G6a's offer):
- contract-scan.ts:412 becomes `...withSpentBy(undefined, spentBy)`, and :220 stops carrying `kept?.spentBy`.
- Update the comments at :12-13 and :107-111, and architecture.md:148 and :419.
- Replace the fold test with one that checks the session view holds no spender after a reading that named none. My test's `keptAcrossReads === false` half does that.
- The cost, checked in a copy: the fold test fails ("expected 'Received' to be 'Already in your private balance'"). A spend that another read folds in first (a Lovejoin due withdraw's readContract, or a Send review's) is read as received again. It then ranks first for fundings and the stealth mint, which is the link gap-g9#1 fixed.

Either way, the lead should take the question to the owner with this cost, since the decision's "no record" doesn't match the code.

findings.title: sign-and-publish runs a third-party action after the key is imported and unlocked in gpg-agent
findings.scenario: The new job imports RELEASE_GPG_KEY and signs with the passphrase through loopback. gpg-agent then holds the unlocked key for its cache time (default-cache-ttl, 10 minutes). The same job, user and agent socket then run softprops/action-gh-release, third-party JavaScript holding the write token. dependabot.yml now proposes a new pin for that action every month. If a bad upstream commit reaches the pin through such a bump, the action can, during a release, have the agent sign a swapped binary with no passphrase and upload it with its .asc. That passes RELEASE.md's gpg --verify, which is b1#3's own harm. finalize-release had the same exposure, so it isn't a regression. But the split leaves this one third-party step beside the key, and the class fix would close it.
findings.who: stranger (whoever controls softprops/action-gh-release's code at a SHA the owner merges)
findings.evidence: release.yml:226 `printf '%s\n' "$RELEASE_GPG_KEY" | gpg --batch --yes --import`; :234 `printf '%s' "$GPG_PASSPHRASE" | gpg --batch --yes --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-fd 0 \`; :239 `uses: softprops/action-gh-release@3bb12739… # v2 (v2.6.2)` in the same job, with :264 `GITHUB_TOKEN`. workflows.test.ts's BUILD_USES (:151) doesn't count it as building, so no rule covers it.
findings.fix: Simplest: publish with GitHub's own preinstalled CLI in a run: step (`gh release create "$TAG" --draft --generate-notes --notes-file … <8 files>` with GH_TOKEN and the tag through env:), so no third-party code shares the key's job. Or end the signing step with `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent` and delete ~/.gnupg. Or move publishing to its own job with contents: write and no secrets, fed the .asc files as artifacts. Add a workflows.test.ts rule: no third-party `uses:` in a job that holds RELEASE_GPG_KEY.
findings.owner_question: Replace softprops with `gh release create`, or keep it and wipe the agent and keyring before it runs?

verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD (69d001e8). The finding holds, and the harm is wider than it says.

What the job does:
- The sign-and-publish job (environment: release :193, contents: write :194-195) imports the key at release.yml:218-226 (`printf '%s\n' "$RELEASE_GPG_KEY" | gpg --batch --yes --import`).
- It signs the four files at :228-236 (`printf '%s' "$GPG_PASSPHRASE" | gpg --batch --yes --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-fd 0 ... --detach-sign`).
- Then :238-264 runs `softprops/action-gh-release@3bb12739c298aeb8a4eeaf626c5b8d85266b0e65 # v2 (v2.6.2)` with `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`.
- Nothing in between stops gpg-agent or removes the keyring.

The agent cache, checked locally (GnuPG 2.4.8; GitHub's Ubuntu 24.04 runners ship 2.4.x):
- `gpgconf --list-options gpg-agent` gives default-cache-ttl 600 s and max-cache-ttl 7200 s.
- With a throwaway passphrase-protected key and a fresh agent, a sign with no passphrase (`--pinentry-mode error`) is refused ("signing failed: No pinentry"). That is the control.
- I then ran release.yml's own sign script, cut from the file and run as written.
- After it, a separate process with no GPG_PASSPHRASE and gpg told never to ask signed a swapped archive, and `gpg --verify` printed `Good signature`.
- Ending the sign step with `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent` made the same later sign fail again.
- Not run on a hosted runner: the agent daemonizes, and the runner kills orphan processes only at job end (release.yml:10's own comment relies on a process outliving its step). softprops is a node action on the same VM, user and HOME, so it reaches the same socket.

Wider than the finding (inferred from the public 2025 tj-actions/changed-files payload, not run here):
- The `runner` user on hosted runners has passwordless sudo.
- The job's secrets sit in Runner.Worker's memory for the whole job, and that payload read them with sudo.
- So a bad softprops could take RELEASE_GPG_KEY and GPG_PASSPHRASE themselves, not only a 10-minute signing window.
- That also means the finding's second fix (stop the agent, delete the keyring) does not close it on its own.

No guard catches it:
- BUILD_USES (workflows.test.ts:151) doesn't list softprops, so the "one job that builds nothing" test (:238-249) passes.
- pinned() accepts any 40-hex SHA.
- dependabot.yml groups every action into one monthly PR, so a softprops bump rides along with GitHub's own bumps.
- The owner's approval only starts the job; the draft gate inspects no code.
- Swapped archives plus a re-signed hashes.txt pass RELEASE.md:37-47's checks.

Against DECISIONS:
- b1#3 (C1 OK) decided one sign-and-publish job and is silent on third-party code inside it.
- b1#5 accepted softprops after the key with only a SHA pin (comment at workflows.test.ts:60-67).
- B13 gives that pin a monthly update path.
- Not a regression: at 984ff48f, finalize-release imported the key, signed hashes.txt (passphrase on argv), then ran the same SHA.
- The repo's own precedent is data-layer-deploy.yml's vps job: it holds DEPLOY_SSH_KEY, runs only actions/download-artifact, and has a "Forget the key" step.

Severity is low: there's no reachable harm today, since the pinned code is fixed. It needs an upstream compromise, the owner merging that bump, and a release run.

What holds: the builds hold no secret and get a read-only token, the key comes in on stdin and the passphrase on a file descriptor through env:, and all 12 existing workflows tests pass on HEAD.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. Replace softprops with GitHub's preinstalled `gh` in a run: step of the same job. This is the class fix. The sketch below passed in the copy:
```yaml
      - name: Create GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          printf '%s\n' "### New Release: $GITHUB_REF_NAME" "" \
              "This release includes binaries and checksums for Linux, Windows, and macOS." "" \
              "Get the [release key here](https://github.com/logical-mechanism/Seedelf-Wallet/blob/main/util/pubkeys/seedelfwallet.asc)." "" \
              'Thank you for using `seedelf-cli`.' "" \
              "If you encounter any issues, please report them [here](https://github.com/logical-mechanism/Seedelf-Wallet/issues)." \
            | gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --verify-tag --draft \
                --generate-notes --notes-file - \
                seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli-linux.tar.gz seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli-linux.tar.gz.asc \
                seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli-windows.zip seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli-windows.zip.asc \
                seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli-macos.tar.gz seedelf-platform/seedelf-cli-macos.tar.gz.asc \
                hashes.txt hashes.txt.asc
```
- `--repo` is needed because the job has no checkout.
- The tag comes from $GITHUB_REF_NAME, never an expression, so the "no expression in a script" rule holds.
- Use `github.token`, not `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`. Otherwise the "never say a value in a step that holds a secret" rule flags the printf lines, which carry a $ and no pipe.
- `gh` 2.46 prepends --notes-file to the generated notes.

2. Also end the sign step with `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent`. It's cheap defence in depth, but it is not the fix on its own: sudo can still read the secrets from Runner.Worker's memory.

3. In workflows.test.ts:
- Rewrite "goes with every file the release publishes" (:262-280), which reads softprops' `files: |` block. Read `gh release create`'s arguments instead: find the release.yml run block holding it, join the `\` line continuations, and keep the args matching `^(seedelf-platform/[\w.-]+|hashes\.txt(\.asc)?)$`.
- Add the two docs#5 tests from the test field. The class rule covers every job holding a secret other than GITHUB_TOKEN, and the vps job already passes it.

Checked in the copy with 1 + 2 + 3: workflows.test.ts passes 14 of 14, the YAML parses (Ruby), and each step's script passes bash -n.

4. With option 1, RELEASE.md doesn't change, and Dependabot no longer bumps anything that runs beside the key. If the owner prefers a separate publish job (contents: write, no secrets, fed the .asc files as artifacts):
- the sign job drops to contents: read;
- RELEASE.md:53 ("reads the key and can write") changes;
- the test at :238-249 ("the only one that can write") changes.

No privacy-policy entry is needed: this is CI only. Owner question: replace softprops with `gh release create` (recommended), or move publishing to a job of its own? Stopping the agent alone doesn't settle it.

findings.scenario: RELEASE.md, a public page, says as fact that 'Only that job reads the key, which is held in the repository's release environment, and only once a maintainer approves it'. Once the branch merges, that's published at once. Until the owner makes the environment, adds the reviewer and tag rule, moves both secrets and deletes the repository ones, the key is a repository secret any workflow can name. findings.owner_question: Set up the release environment before the merge?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding's facts are right, but what it describes is the decided order of steps. It is not a defect in the tree.

What is true, checked on HEAD 69d001e8:
- RELEASE.md:5 says, word for word, "Only that job reads the key, which is held in the repository's `release` environment, and only once a maintainer approves it."
- release.yml:182-184 admits the state before setup: "Until that environment is made, GitHub makes an empty one at the first run, and the job takes the repository's secrets, unguarded, as the builds did."
- So until the owner makes the environment, the key is a repository secret, and a tag would run sign-and-publish (:187-264, `environment: release` at :193) with no approval.

Why it's decided, not a bug:
- DECISIONS b1#3 OWNER line: "C1 = OK. The owner creates the 'release' environment by hand; you write the workflow change (...) so it's ready."
- The recommendation it accepts is "Yes, in two steps. The owner: a 'release' environment ... Then the workflow".
- g7to10 step 2: "The owner creates the 'release' environment. Then b1#3's release.yml PR".
- review-51.md:234: "Only the owner can make the environment; the workflow change can follow."
- The fixer's handoff (round1.json, G8, b1#3 "left") lists the owner's steps (1)-(5), then "(6) Merge, then tag", with what goes wrong in each other order. The finding's fix is this same handoff.

Guards the finder missed:
- RELEASE.md:53 puts the environment's setup inside "Making a release", before the version-bump block. :77 makes approving the job a step ("approve its `sign-and-publish` job (*Review deployments* on the run's page)"). So an owner following the doc for 0.7.1 sets it up before tagging.
- The owner's own plan (memory, chunk-51-whole-review.md:21) is "release the CLI first (needs the `release` environment, C1, before the tag)".
- sign-and-publish makes only a draft (release.yml:242 `draft: true`), so even a tag pushed before setup publishes nothing without the owner.
- b1#3's threat, a build script taking the key, is closed by the workflow alone: no build job names a secret.

Can anyone reach it? No. Main's release.yml (git show main:.github/workflows/release.yml:3-6) and HEAD's run only when a tag matching `*.*.*` is pushed, and no tag is due before the merge. Between a merge and the owner's setup, nothing reads the key, and environment settings can't be seen from outside. Who: nobody. No funds and no user action are involved.

What holds in code, run in a copy: in all five workflows, only release.yml's sign-and-publish names RELEASE_GPG_KEY or GPG_PASSPHRASE (:220, :230). Only that job has `environment: release`, it builds nothing, and it is the only job that can write. workflows.test.ts's b1#3 tests pass.

What's left: the owner's memory plan says "before the tag", not before the merge. If the owner merges before steps 1-5, RELEASE.md:5 is ahead of the settings for that window, with no run in it. Also, 02b9c1fe's commit message names b1#3 but not the owner's steps. Both are handoff points, not tree defects.
verdicts.fix_notes:
No change in the tree.

For the lead:
- Copy b1#3's owner steps (1)-(5) from round1.json (G8, b1#3, "left") into the whole-review PR's body, marked "before merging": the 'release' environment, yourself as reviewer with Prevent self-review off, the tag rule `*.*.*`, the two environment secrets, then deleting the repository's two. Doing them first costs nothing, because main's release.yml runs only on a tag. RELEASE.md:5 is then true the moment it lands.
- The owner's own plan ("before the tag") also works, since nothing runs in between. It only leaves the public line ahead of the settings for that window.
- Don't hedge RELEASE.md:5 with "once set up". :53 says what the setup is and :77 depends on it, so a hedge would be out of date the day after setup.
- Optional, after the environment exists: release.yml:182-184's "Until that environment is made ..." sentence can be cut. It's still accurate as a conditional, so it can also stay.

findings.title: No CI runs seedelf-verification/test-tools.sh, though this round put new verdict logic in check.sh and scan-diag.py
findings.scenario: The tools' tests need no Lean and take about ten seconds; this round grew them from 50 checks to 80. No workflow runs them, and web-wallet.yml's covered filter rightly leaves seedelf-verification/ out. So a later PR that changes only check.sh, scan-diag.py, accepted.txt or expected-failures.txt merges with no check. So does one that changes PolicyBurn.lean or PolicyMint.lean, which test-tools.sh embeds by line and column. EXPECTED or the accepted list could then pass a failure, or flag a good run, until someone runs the script by hand.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn test-tools .github/` finds nothing; test-tools.sh:1-3 'no Lean, no Lake, no systemd, about ten seconds'; round1.json G10 notes 5: 'If either file changes, that test will want the console recorded again.'
findings.fix: A small job, for example in continuous-integration.yml or a new workflow with a paths filter on seedelf-verification/**/*.sh, *.py, *.txt and Seedelf/Policy*.lean. It would be `bash seedelf-verification/test-tools.sh` on ubuntu-latest (bash, python3). No Lean build, so docs PRs stay fast.
findings.owner_question: Should CI run the proofs' tool tests on PRs that touch them?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 69d001e8. I found no guard it missed.

1. Nothing runs the script. Inside .github/, `grep -rn test-tools .github/` finds nothing. Across the whole tree, `git grep test-tools HEAD` finds only README.md:183, review-51.md:113 and :136, and the script itself. No git hook, husky, lefthook or pre-commit config exists. check.sh and Audit/run-all.sh never call it.

2. No workflow picks up these files.
   - continuous-integration.yml runs on every pull request, but only Aiken (:24-29).
   - data-layer.yml has a paths filter: seedelf-data/** plus some seedelf-platform files.
   - release.yml runs on tags, and data-layer-deploy.yml on workflow_dispatch.
   - web-wallet.yml's covered program (:72) skips every file the script reads. I ran the exact awk program on check.sh, test-tools.sh, tally.py, expected-failures.txt, Audit/count.py, Audit/run-all.sh, Audit/diag/scan-diag.py, Audit/diag/accepted.txt, Audit/diag/selftest/*.txt and Seedelf/PolicyBurn.lean and PolicyMint.lean: "skips" for all of them. Even when the check does run, none of its jobs calls the script. So a pull request touching only these files gets Aiken and a green "Web Wallet required".

3. The round raised the stakes. In ec3e388f (G10), check.sh gained expected() (HEAD :326-467) and its use in the loop (:482-541): a failed build that matches expected-failures.txt now reads EXPECTED and exits 0. scan-diag.py gained accepted() and lean_name() (:168-203) and the `new` LOOK rule (:318-358). Before, these tools could only fail loudly; now they can pass quietly. I ran test-tools.sh on git-archive copies: the base 984ff48f gives 50 ok, HEAD gives 80 ok, about 10.8 s, "PASS: the tools hold". So "50 checks to 80" is exact.

4. The script pins the Policy sources by position. test-tools.sh:367-381 records the console by line and column: PolicyBurn.lean 28:89, 31:93, 34:101, 37:103, and PolicyMint.lean 32:99, 37:101. Those match the sources today (theorems at :28, :31, :34, :37 and :32, :37). The G10 fixer's note 5 in round1.json says the same: "If either file changes, that test will want the console recorded again."

5. The scenario reproduces, in scratch copies:
   - Dropping check.sh:461's count check (`if False and (valid, falsified) != (ev, ef):`) gives "FAIL a counted theorem's ✅ missing reads EXPECTED, exit 0". That is EXPECTED passing a real failure.
   - Adding one line to PolicyBurn.lean's module doc comment gives "FAIL Seedelf.PolicyBurn's recorded failure reads FAILED, exit 1". That is the tool test going stale.
   Each pull request would merge green.

6. It isn't a decided behaviour. The DECISIONS.md lines for G8, B12 and B11 don't cover a job for test-tools.sh. B12 chose a covered-filter term over a new job, but only because an existing job already runs the .hex test; nothing runs test-tools.sh. web-wallet.yml:42-43 keeps Lean and docs out of the 13-minute wallet check, not out of CI as a whole. The CI-speed rule asks for a parallel job, which a 10 s job is. Chunk 51 covered CI (its B1 lane and G8 group), so this is in scope.

Severity is low: a missing check with no harm reachable today, caused by nobody. The real ./check.sh still judges the real console, so a stale fixture is a false alarm, and an expected() regression needs a later bad edit. README.md:183 says only that `bash test-tools.sh` checks the rules, and doesn't claim CI runs it, so no claim is wider than the code. The finder's cited ranges match HEAD; check.sh's block starts at :326, not :331.
verdicts.fix_notes:
This is the owner's call: should CI run the proofs' tool tests? If yes, there are two shapes. Both pass the pinning test below.

(A) Recommended: a second, parallel job in .github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml, after `build`:

  verification-tools:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: The proofs' tools' own test
        run: bash seedelf-verification/test-tools.sh

The workflow already runs on every pull request and already has `permissions: contents: read`. actions/checkout is first-party, so it needs no SHA pin. The job runs no compiler and holds no secret, so it passes workflows.test.ts's rules on tokens, secrets and builders. It adds no wall time: about 11 s beside Aiken's check, and the script works from the repository root, because it finds its folder from $0. There's no path list to keep in sync, so a file the script comes to read is covered with no edit. Python 3 and GNU coreutils are on the runner, and lake, systemd-run and z3 are the script's own stand-ins.

(B) Or a new workflow .github/workflows/verification-tools.yml with `on: pull_request: paths:` set to "seedelf-verification/**/*.sh", "seedelf-verification/**/*.py", "seedelf-verification/**/*.txt", "seedelf-verification/Seedelf/PolicyBurn.lean", "seedelf-verification/Seedelf/PolicyMint.lean" and the workflow file itself. Give it the same job, plus top-level `permissions: contents: read`. Never make it a required check: a check that a path filter skips never reports, and that holds the pull request (web-wallet.yml:3-8).

With either shape, add the test below to seedelf-platform/seedelf-web-wallet/extension/tests/workflows.test.ts. It reads the file list from test-tools.sh's own `$TOOLS/` reads. It runs only when the wallet check runs, which includes any workflow edit and main's run. Under (B), a new `$TOOLS/` read whose file the filter misses is caught on main, after the merge, which is one more reason for (A). If (B) is chosen, also say in web-wallet.yml's covered comment (:34-49) that the proofs' tools have their own check.

Separately: the recorded PolicyBurn and PolicyMint console (test-tools.sh:363-385) goes stale whenever either source moves a line. Its comment could say to record it again from the next default run's console, as G10's note 5 says.

No change to wallet code, strings or the privacy policy.
