findings.title: B15 (b) makes the stealth mint take a never-mixed box of the wallet's own session first, and the mint's note then says it keeps the Seedelf apart
findings.scenario: A private session's chain stopped before its boxes were mixed (a lock mid-chain, say). The user presses Bring one back anyway, which warns only that the deposit is tied to the private balance. Or the pool is retired, and the box comes back by itself (privacy.md:466). The box comes back classed box:<tx>: withdrawOne sets no origin (lovejoin.ts:8085-8086), depositAccountOf returns undefined for a session's chain (lovejoin.ts:2364), and classOf gives boxFrom (activity.ts:797-798). Later the user creates a Seedelf from the private balance, which also holds a 20 ₳ payment from a friend. Purpose::Mint now ranks Lovejoin 0, so step 1 takes the box alone. The new Seedelf's mint then spends an output anyone can trace to that session's deposit and funding, and through a Make private to Account 0. In 1.9.1 the friend's payment went first. The form meanwhile says 'Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account' (en.json:1464). A private pool start uses the same rank.
findings.who: user (one press), or nobody (a retired pool brings such boxes back by itself); the wallet's default pick makes the link
findings.evidence: build.rs:2484-2486 `Purpose::Mint => match class.origin { Lovejoin => 0, Received => 1, ...`; lovejoin.ts:8085 `const own = received ? receivedIn(built.txHash) : boxFrom(built.txHash);` with origin left undefined unless spent||received; lovejoin.ts:2364 `if (chain) return chain.session === undefined ? (chain.account ?? 0) : undefined;`. G4a1 named exactly this in round1.json (notes 3, siblings: 'a box the wallet's own session deposited, brought back anyway without a mix, still classes box:<tx>. Under (b) the stealth mint takes it first'). Neither G1a nor G6a built it. DECISIONS' cross-cutting note (6) covered only a stranger's box.
findings.fix: In withdrawOne, class a box that the wallet's own session deposited and no mix moved as that session's money. The chain's `session` gives sessionClass(i), as PRIV-3's tiedOrigin already does for a public account's deposit. Class an unsure box unknownIn(tx). Mint then ranks both after received money. Or have Purpose::Mint rank first only boxes known to be mixed. Add a mint test with a never-mixed session box beside a received payment.
findings.owner_question: Did B15's 'a box back from Lovejoin first' mean mixed boxes only? If so, which class should a never-mixed own box carry: its session's, or Unknown?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD (69d001e8). Every line it cites matches HEAD, and the value is wrong from start to finish. I looked for a guard and found none.

1. The ranking changed this round. `git diff 984ff48f..HEAD` on seedelf-core/src/build.rs:2484-2486 flips `Purpose::Mint` from `Received => 0, Lovejoin => 1` to `Lovejoin => 0, Received => 1`. Step 1 of `apart` (build.rs:2828-2833) sorts single UTxOs by `(last(u), purpose.rank(&class(u)))`, then by lovelace, and takes the first that builds. So a box that pays alone now beats a received payment. The stealth mint uses this ranking (wasm lib.rs:2490, `mint_apart`), and so does a private pool start (lib.rs:2801, `build_launch` → `launch_apart`). On 984ff48f the friend's payment went first, as the finding says.

2. A private session's box comes back classed as a plain box.
   - withdrawOne, lovejoin.ts:8079-8086: `deposited = depositAccountOf(s, box)`, then `const own = received ? receivedIn(built.txHash) : boxFrom(built.txHash); origin = spent || received ? merged(...) : undefined;`
   - depositAccountOf (:2363-2368) returns undefined for a session: `if (chain) return chain.session === undefined ? (chain.account ?? 0) : undefined;`, and the MixEntry fallback does the same. So `ties` stays undefined.
   - `received` is false. someoneElsesOf (:2671-2674) runs through depositsOf (:2095-2102), which skips any box a recorded chain made (`recorded`). After a restore, a deposit paid by a one-time key counts as `ours`.
   - With the box paying its own way back, `spent` is undefined. `back` (:8171) is then `tiedOrigin(w, undefined)`, which is {}. settleWithdrawing (:8287-8290) writes the same.
   - activity.ts `sent` stores a lovejoin-withdraw entry with no origin. classOf (activity.ts:797-798) turns that into `boxFrom(tx)`, which is {id: box:<tx>, origin: "lovejoin"}.
   - From there: readContract (script-spend.ts:246) → mint.ts:113-114 → `histories(Purpose::Mint)` gives rank 0. Nothing in mint.ts or readContract filters boxes out, and spentHistories writes no review note for a single class.

3. Ways a user gets such a box (all checked):
   - Bring one back anyway. withdrawNowNow (lovejoin.ts:7409-7417) only warns with lj.privacy.boxChainStopped or boxUnmixed.
   - A private Bootstrap's own Bring one back. sessions.ts:5505-5515 records `session: built.index, bootstrap: true` with its deposit, and its held box is taken with no `anyway` at all. This path is wider than the finding states.
   - Bring every box back now, and the retired pools' run, which brings boxes back unasked. privacy.md:456-459 says these bring never-mixed boxes back.

4. Claims now wider than the code. Both changed this round:
   - en.json:1464 mint.privacy.fromPrivate: "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account".
   - privacy.md:107: "No payer knows a box back from a mix, so a box that pays alone goes first".
   - The UTxOs screen tags this UTxO "Back from Lovejoin" (historyTags).

5. The wallet's own precedent goes the other way. PRIV-3's tiedOrigin (lovejoin.ts:2378) already classes a public account's never-mixed deposit box as box+public:n (origin own, Mint rank 3), tested at lovejoin-release-rules.test.ts:457. The private-session case is the gap.

6. Nobody decided or built this.
   - G4a1 flagged it (round1.json, G4a1 note 3).
   - G6a's note relies only on "a stranger's box brought back as receivedIn". G1a doesn't mention it.
   - DECISIONS cross-cutting note (6) covers only a stranger's box.
   - G4a1's own test pins today's behaviour: tests/lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:256-257, `expect((await historyOf(t, own.txHash))?.origin).toBeUndefined()`, under the title "the wallet's own deposit's as a box back from Lovejoin".

7. A related problem that predates this round: Fund ranks the same box as Lovejoin (2) instead of another session's money (5).

Run: I copied the tree, kept its WebAssembly (the pkg is newer than every Rust source), and ran a Vitest test with three cases. All three fail on HEAD: the class is box:<w> with origin lovejoin, and the stealth mint spends the box's way back, not the friend's 20 ₳. With a candidate fix applied in the copy, all three pass, and lovejoin-someone-else's pinned `.toBeUndefined()` fails as expected. I deleted the copy afterwards. No cargo target was made.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. Fix withdrawOne (lovejoin.ts:8079-8086). This is PRIV-3's tiedOrigin for a private depositor.
   - Next to `deposited = depositAccountOf(s, box)`, find the private session whose deposit put the box there with no mix since. Use the lookups depositAccountOf already makes, keeping `session` where it returns undefined:
     - a chain with `c.deposit === box.txHash`;
     - or a MixEntry whose deposit (or a Bootstrap's or seed's id) is the box's tx.
   - After a restore, use an `origins[box.txHash]` with mixed false whose `inputs` include one-time key i. Give oneTimeKeys, or a sibling of it, a key-to-index map.
   - Then set `origin = merged([own, sessionClass(i), ...spent class, ...ties.map(madePrivate)])`. Its origin is "session" (REACH), and the UTxOs screen tags it "Back from Lovejoin" plus "Private session N".
   - Set it as Withdrawing `origin`, so settleWithdrawing (:8287-8290) writes the same class.
   - Effects: Mint ranks it 4, Pay 1, Fund 0 for that session's own top-up and 5 for another session's. That also fixes the older Fund ordering.

2. For a box the wallet can't place, optionally use `unknownIn(tx)` instead of boxFrom. This covers no record and Koios not asked, or no key matched, and not someone else's. Replace boxFrom, as `received` already does. Never merge the two: merged() picks "lovejoin" over "unknown". Trade-off: Unknown is tier 0, so Pay may merge it earlier than it merges a box.

3. Another way (the owner's call): leave the classes alone and make core's Purpose::Mint rank 0 only boxes known to be mixed. That needs a new origin or a flag carried in from TypeScript, which is a bigger change.

4. Tests:
   - Add the test below (tests/still-1-never-mixed-box.test.ts).
   - Change tests/lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:256-257 (and its title) to expect the own deposit's box as `box:<w>+session:0`, origin "session".
   - Leave the core test a_stealth_mint_takes_a_box_that_pays_alone_before_received_money as it is.

5. Docs:
   - privacy.md's Co-spending list (:166-171): one line saying a box no mix moved since a private session's deposit carries that session's history, as a public account's carries the account's.
   - No new record is kept (origin is already sealed), so no policy entry.
   - The en.json:1464 and privacy.md:107 claims hold again once such boxes aren't plain boxes.

6. Owner question: does B15's "a box back from Lovejoin" mean a mixed box only? If so, should an own box that was never mixed take its session's class (the fix above), or Unknown?

verdicts.evidence:
I tried to refute it and couldn't. Every step reads as the finding says, on HEAD 69d001e8. Nothing was run.

1. The rank. seedelf-core/src/build.rs:2484-2486 has `Purpose::Mint => match class.origin { Lovejoin => 0, Received => 1,`. At 984ff48f it was Received 0, Lovejoin 1.
   - Step 1 sorts single UTxOs by (last, rank, lovelace) (one_more :2720-2747, called at :2830-2834), so every box that pays alone is tried before any received payment.
   - The stealth mint takes this order (wasm/src/lib.rs:2490 `histories(Purpose::Mint, …)`), and so does a pool start from the private balance (lib.rs:2801; lovejoin/launch.rs:791).

2. The class an own never-mixed box comes back with.
   - lovejoin.ts:2363-2364: `if (chain) return chain.session === undefined ? (chain.account ?? 0) : undefined;`. A session's deposit gives no tie.
   - :8075: `received` is true only for someoneElses. A recorded chain's box is `known`, so depositsOf (:2095-2101) and someoneElsesOf (:2671-2675) never count it.
   - :8085-8086: `own = received ? receivedIn(..) : boxFrom(..)`, and `origin = spent || received ? … : undefined`.
   - When the box pays its own way back (paid undefined), back.origin is tiedOrigin(tx, undefined) = {} (:8171). activity.ts:385-443 then writes no origin, and classOf (activity.ts:797-798) returns `boxFrom(entry.txHash)`, origin "lovejoin", which is Mint rank 0.
   - A test pins this. tests/lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:256-257 brings back the wallet's own session-0 deposit (`paidBy(oneTimeKey(t, 0))`) anyway and asserts `origin` toBeUndefined, which classes as box:<tx>. The test's comment at :252-253 says the stealth mint takes a box first.

3. Reach.
   - cuts() (:6094-6120) ends a chain whose progress went at a lock, a closed browser or an update ("nothing sends the rest").
   - sortOut (:6209) holds its deposit's boxes as unmixed.
   - withdrawNow refuses an unmixed box only `!anyway` (:7412), then calls withdrawOne (:7478).
   - Bring every box back (:7765) and a retired pool's run take the same path. sortOut's `waits` holds nothing in a retired pool. A restored wallet's own deposit judged by its one-time key does too (the test above).
   - Legacy box:<tx> entries already in histories, from 1.8.0's retirement run or 1.9.1 anyway presses, now move ahead of received money too.

4. Nothing warns or catches it later.
   - The anyway question (lovejoin.anyway.privacy.stopped) says only that it ties the deposit to the private balance.
   - historiesNote (histories.ts:188-236) says nothing when only one class is spent.
   - The UTxOs tag reads "Back from Lovejoin" for a mixed box too.
   - This round widened the claims:
     - en.json:1464 (was "Only money others paid you keeps…") now says "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account".
     - privacy.md:81 and :107 say such a box "hides the payer from people reading the chain".

5. Not built, and not decided.
   - lovejoin.ts has no sessionClass or unknownIn.
   - round1.json G4a1 note 3 and its siblings name this exact residual. G1a's and G6a's items cover only a stranger's box (received).
   - DECISIONS' B15 line and cross-cutting note (6) don't decide an own never-mixed box. Core's own doc gives the reason as "which no payer knows", so this is (b) breaking something else, not a decided behaviour.

Impact:
- Who: the user (one warned press of Bring one back anyway, or Bring every box back), or nobody (a retired pool's run, or the legacy entries). The wallet's default pick then makes the link.
- What's lost: the new Seedelf, or a private pool start, is tied for anyone reading the chain to the session's one-time account, its activity and its funding. Where the funding was money made private, it's tied to the public account, which is the link the stealth mint exists to avoid and which its note says it avoids.
- Against 1.9.1: the pick changed only where a received payment also pays alone. 1.9.1 already ranked the box ahead of Unknown, Own and Session. The wider claim is wrong in every case.
- No funds are lost and no stranger is needed. That makes it medium on the brief's scale (a privacy link the wallet makes by default, and a claim wider than the code), at the narrow end of reach.
- Minor mis-cite: the retired pools' behaviour is privacy.md:458; :466 is the restore line.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. lovejoin.ts: add depositSessionOf(s, box) next to depositAccountOf (:2362). It returns the session whose chain's deposit made the box: `c.deposit === box.txHash && c.session !== undefined`, or the mix entry whose deposit it is, with entry.session. Gate it on "no mix moved it since", using unmixedOf/notMixedYet's notion. A box a session chain made short of its leaves is still traceable, so it counts too.

2. withdrawOne (:8075-8086), when the box isn't someone else's and is such a box:
   - Set `own = merged([boxFrom(tx), sessionClass(i)])`. Its origin is session: Mint ranks it 4, a top-up of that session 0, another funding 5, Pay 1.
   - Set `origin` even when !spent, and keep merging spent.class on the private-paid path. Store it in s.withdrawing.origin, which settleWithdrawing already prefers (:8288).
   - After a restore, for a deposit judged the phrase's own by a one-time key: have oneTimeKeys return keyHash→index, so the box classes as sessionClass(i).
   - Otherwise, and for an unsure box brought back anyway, use `unknownIn(tx)` alone. Never merge it with boxFrom: merged()'s REACH (histories.ts:94) puts lovejoin ahead of unknown, so the merged class would still be the mint's first pick.

3. Tests:
   - Flip lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:257 to expect the session class.
   - Add a mint_test.rs case: a box classed `box:X+session:0` (Origin::Session) beside a 20 ₳ received payment must make the mint spend the payment. Keep a_stealth_mint_takes_a_box_that_pays_alone_before_received_money for mixed boxes.
   - Add an extension test: a cut session chain's box brought back anyway, then a stealth mint from the private balance with a received payment that pays alone.

4. Legacy box:<tx> entries (1.8.0's retirement run, 1.9.1 anyway presses) can't be re-judged on the device once the chain record has gone. Either say so in privacy.md, or, as the owner decides, rank first for Mint only boxes with positive evidence of a mix. That means a mark written at withdraw time when the box is a leaf or Koios said a mix made it, with unmarked box:<tx> keeping 1.9.1's place after received money. That needs a core Origin or class-spelling change in core and WebAssembly.

5. Words: once the classing lands, en.json:1464 and privacy.md:81, :107 and :170 hold for what the wallet calls a box. Add one clause to privacy.md's Bring one back anyway and retired-pool lines: a box brought back without a mix is then spent as its session's money. No new UI string is needed.

6. Owner question, as the finding put it: did B15's "a box back from Lovejoin first" mean mixed boxes only, and should an own never-mixed box carry its session's class or Unknown?
verdicts.test:
Extension (Vitest), built on lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts's fixture at :231-258:
1. Give the wallet a session 0 and a box A whose deposit was paid by oneTimeKey(t, 0). Alternatively, record a session chain whose deposit landed and cut it (no progress, so cuts() ends it).
2. Run lj.status, then lj.withdrawNow("preprod", inAda(A), true).
3. Add a 20 ₳ received payment to the contract view.
4. Build a stealth mint from the private balance (mint-build with from "seedelf").

Today the mint spends the box's withdraw output alone; under 1.9.1's order it took the payment. After the fix, the output's class has origin "session" (or "unknown" when the session can't be told) and the mint spends the received payment.

Core (mint_test.rs): available = a 20 ₳ received payment, a 9.71 ₳ UTxO classed box:X+session:0 (Origin::Session), and 1,000 ₳ made private. build::mint_apart with Purpose::Mint must spend the received payment alone. A 9.71 ₳ UTxO classed box:Y (Origin::Lovejoin) beside it is still taken first.

findings.title: The policy and privacy.md say Translate never gets the recovery phrase, but Restore's and Create's word suggestions still translate
findings.scenario: Chrome is set to Always translate English pages into German. The user restores a wallet and types each word. While a box is focused, PhraseInput lists up to 5 BIP-39 words that start with what's typed: 'aban' lists 'abandon', the user's own word. Each list is plain page text with no translate="no", so Translate sends those words to Google. Create's confirm step uses the same input. Yet privacy-policy.md:67 now says 'not your recovery phrase: the wallet marks its words not to translate, so Translate neither sends them nor changes them', its 18 November entry says 'Chrome's Translate no longer gets your recovery phrase', and privacy.md:279 says the 24 words are kept out.
findings.who: nobody (Chrome's Translate under the user's own setting); the published claim is wider than the code
findings.evidence:
PhraseGrid.tsx:13 is the only translate="no" (phrase-translate.test.ts asserts that it's the only one, the owner's 'alone'). PhraseInput.tsx:219-234 renders `
    …{word.slice(0, value.length)}{word.slice(value.length)}`. G7a named this sibling in round1 ('PhraseInput's suggestion list … still translates. Named, not changed: the owner said the grid alone'). G8's policy words claim the whole phrase anyway. Not checked in a browser (inferred, as the decision's own premise is).
findings.fix: Either narrow the words: privacy.md:279, privacy-policy.md:67 and the :93 entry would say the words are kept out where Create and Settings show them, and that the restore and confirm boxes' suggestions still translate. Or, as the owner's call, put translate="no" on PhraseInput's suggestion list too and widen phrase-translate.test.ts's allow-list. Also 'the recovery phrase's 24 words' should say 'its words': a restored 12- or 15-word phrase shows in the same grid (G8's note 6).
findings.owner_question: Should B9's 'the grid alone' extend to the restore and confirm boxes' suggestion list, or should the policy say less?

verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD 69d001e8. The tree is clean and was not edited. THE CLAIM (all three lines were written in this round, 484fa70b and 02b9c1fe): - docs/store/privacy-policy.md:67 says Translate gets the page's text "but not your recovery phrase: the wallet marks its words not to translate, so Translate neither sends them nor changes them". - The 18 November entry (:93) says "Chrome's Translate no longer gets your recovery phrase". - docs/privacy.md:279 says "The recovery phrase's 24 words are kept out". - B9's own third reason was to make the policy's row at :13 ("It is never sent anywhere") true under Translate. THE CODE: - PhraseGrid.tsx:13 is the only translate="no" in src/ and index.html, and phrase-translate.test.ts:46 pins that. index.html is lang="en" and has no notranslate meta. - PhraseInput.tsx:147-149: `matches = value && !exact ? list.filter((w) => w.startsWith(value)) : []` and `suggestions = focused ? matches.slice(0, 5) : []`. - :218-235 renders them as plain page text: `
  • {word.slice(0, value.length)}{word.slice(value.length)}
    • `. No element above it carries translate. - Typing "aban" shows "abandon", the person's own word. The input's value comes from the React closure (`accept(word)`), so the words the person ends up with are not changed. The "sends them" half of the claim is the false part. WHERE IT SHOWS (one more place than the finding named): - Restore.tsx:140, with every box. - Create.tsx:183, the confirm step's 3 words. - Settings.tsx:1469, Check recovery phrase. privacy.md's own Copying bullet names it as a place the phrase is typed. - Settings' Show recovery phrase gets entropyToPhrase(entropy) (wallet.ts:417-425), so a restored 12- or 15-word phrase shows in the grid. The "24 words" in privacy.md:279, the PhraseGrid.tsx:9 comment and backlog.md:230 is wrong for those. That part is a nit. HOW MUCH LEAKS: run over bip39 2.2.2's English list, typed letter by letter, 1977 of 2048 words appear in the list at some point. A 24-word phrase typed by hand puts about 23 of its words in it. The other 71 are short words like "act"; for them only the typed prefix shows, in bold. GUARDS LOOKED FOR, NONE FOUND: any translate or notranslate on an ancestor, Screen, index.html or CSS; the list being in a guarded subtree; a paste-only path. A pasted phrase gives exact matches and so no list, but typing is the ordinary path. ROUND HISTORY: PhraseInput.tsx has no diff in the round. G7a's round1 entry already says the list "still translates. Named, not changed: the owner said the grid alone". G8's note 6 raised the 24-word wording, which privacy.md:279 still has. B9's "Where now" named only PhraseGrid, so the owner decided without this sibling in view. The owner's decisions (the grid alone, and docs saying the phrase is kept out) together publish a claim wider than the code. INFERRED, NOT CHECKED IN A BROWSER, as the decision's premise is: that Chrome's Translate translates and sends content added after the first translation. The suggestion list mounts while typing. SEVERITY: medium, under the rubric's "a claim wider than the code" (the published Web Store policy). Who: nobody; it is Chrome's Translate under the user's own setting. TEST: a vitest test in a copy of the tree fails on HEAD. It passes once translate="no" is on the suggestions'
      , and phrase-translate.test.ts:46's "alone" allow-list then fails, as the finding predicted. The copy and its target were deleted afterwards.
verdicts.fix_notes:
This is the owner's call: does B9's "grid alone" reach the list of words suggested under the phrase boxes?

(b) EXTEND B9, the change that fits B9's own reason that "the secret itself goes to Google":
- Add translate="no" to the <ul className="suggestions"> at PhraseInput.tsx:219 alone, not the <ol> at :97. That way the "Word N" labels and phrase.notOnList keep translating.
- Widen phrase-translate.test.ts:46 to ["src/ui/components/PhraseGrid.tsx", "src/ui/components/PhraseInput.tsx"]. Reword its header, its test name and its "alone" wording.
- Reword PhraseGrid.tsx:4-9 ("the only thing in the wallet that is") and backlog.md:230 ("24 words alone").
- Add the test below as the pin.
- The policy's :67 and :93 words then hold as written. No new dated entry is needed, since 18 November already says Translate doesn't get the phrase.

(a) NARROW THE WORDS, no code change:
- privacy-policy.md:67 and the :93 entry say the words are kept out where the wallet shows them (Create's first step, Settings' Show recovery phrase). While a phrase is typed (Restore, Check recovery phrase, Create's confirm step), the words suggested under each box are page text and go to Google with it.
- privacy.md:279 says the same.
- The :13 row ("It is never sent anywhere") needs the same qualifier or a pointer to the Translate paragraph.
- Turn the test below round to pin the narrower claim.

EITHER WAY:
- privacy.md:279's "The recovery phrase's 24 words" becomes "the recovery phrase's words". A restored 12- or 15-word phrase shows in the same grid (G8's note 6).
- Name Settings' Check recovery phrase (Settings.tsx:1469) beside Restore and Create's confirm step. The finding left it out.
- docs/backlog.md:31 still lists "the recovery phrase under Chrome Translate" as an open owner call (❓). Delete that line in whichever PR settles this.

verdicts.evidence:
I checked this on web-wallet/whole-review-fixes at HEAD (69d001e8). The finding holds, and it misses a third place where the leak happens. **The code** - `src/ui/components/PhraseInput.tsx:219-235` draws the suggestions as `
    ` holding `
  • {word.slice(0, value.length)}{word.slice(value.length)}
    • `. Neither element has a `translate` attribute. - The list appears whenever a box is focused and what's typed is the start of a word but not a whole word (`:147-149`, `:218`). - BIP-39 words are unique by their first four letters, so a word typed letter by letter appears as an option before it's taken. The only exceptions are a word that is also the start of others and doesn't make the first five early, like "act", or a phrase that is pasted. - The e2e test at `e2e/extension.spec.ts:219-223` drives exactly this. After three typed letters, it finds `getByRole("option", { name: words[0] })`, the user's full word as page text. - `grep translate= src` matches only `PhraseGrid.tsx:13`, and `tests/phrase-translate.test.ts:42-47` pins that it stays the only one. **Where PhraseInput is used** - `Restore.tsx:140`: the whole 12, 15 or 24 words. - `Create.tsx:183`: the three confirm words. The translated line above them, `create.confirm.enterWords` at `:182`, also gives their positions. - `Settings.tsx:1469-1477`, Check recovery phrase: the live wallet's whole phrase, typed to check a backup. The finding doesn't name this one. - All three run in the wallet's default full tab (`shared/open-in.ts:14`, `DEFAULT_OPEN_IN = "tab"`), the same page as the grid that B9 fixed. **The claims** - `docs/store/privacy-policy.md:67`: "but not your recovery phrase: the wallet marks its words not to translate, so Translate neither sends them nor changes them". - The 18 November entry at `:93`: "Chrome's Translate no longer gets your recovery phrase". - `docs/privacy.md:279`: "The recovery phrase's 24 words are kept out". - The policy's row at `:13` still says the phrase "is never sent anywhere". - None of these is narrowed anywhere else. `flows.md:48` and `:106` describe the suggestions and don't mention Translate. **How it happened** - DECISIONS B9: "translate="no" on the phrase grid alone ... privacy.md and the policy's Translate line say the phrase is kept out". Its trace named only `PhraseGrid`'s two uses. - G7a's round1 entry (`[9]/items[3]/siblings`) named the suggestion list as "still translates. Named, not changed". Even so, G7a's own suggested policy words said "never your recovery phrase". - G8 wrote the unqualified claim. - So the decided code and the decided words disagree. That is a claim wider than the code, not a decided behaviour. **The premise** - That Translate sends text added to the page after it loads is the same premise B9 and the policy already rely on: balances, addresses and Seedelf names all arrive after the first render. - I didn't check it in a browser, and neither did B9. **Impact** - Who can cause it: nobody hostile. It needs the user's own Translate, offered or set to Always translate, in a language the wallet doesn't speak, and a phrase that is typed rather than pasted. - What leaks: in Restore and in Settings' Check recovery phrase, nearly every word goes to Google, in typing order. In Create's confirm step, three words go, with their positions. - What isn't lost: funds aren't directly at risk, and the value a suggestion fills in comes from the code, not the page text (`accept(word)`), so no wrong words get stored. - What catches it: nothing later in the flow. Restore's paste tip helps only users who paste. - Grade: medium. The published store policy and its dated entry promise more than the code does, about the most sensitive secret the wallet holds. **What holds** - The grid really is marked, in both its shown and dotted-out states. - Inputs' typed values aren't page text. - No other screen shows the phrase's words.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Option 1, preferred, but the owner's call because B9 said "the grid alone". It's one attribute, and the policy's words then become true as written:
- Add `translate="no"` to the `<ul className="suggestions">` at `PhraseInput.tsx:219`. If the list's `aria-label` should stay translatable, put it on each `<li role="option">` at `:221` instead.

- In `tests/phrase-translate.test.ts`, widen the allow-list at `:46` to `["src/ui/components/PhraseGrid.tsx", "src/ui/components/PhraseInput.tsx"]` and update the header (`:1-6`) and the test names.

Simplest is the e2e at `extension.spec.ts:220-221`: `await expect(page.getByRole("listbox")).toHaveAttribute("translate", "no")`, or `getByRole("option").first()` if the attribute goes on each `<li>`. Alternatively, use `screens-wiring-review-fixes.test.ts`'s seam to seed WordBox as focused with a prefix and check the rendered markup.

Option 2, if the owner keeps "the grid alone":

Say the words are kept out where Create and Settings show them, but that while the phrase is typed into Restore, Check recovery phrase or Create's confirm step, the words suggested under each box go to Google with the page, and pasting avoids it for Restore and Check.

Either way (nit): change "the recovery phrase's 24 words" to "its words" in `privacy.md:279`, `backlog.md:230`, `PhraseGrid.tsx:9` and `phrase-translate.test.ts`'s header and test name. A restored 12- or 15-word phrase shows in the same grid in Settings' Show recovery phrase.
verdicts.test:

findings.title: CI's WebAssembly node tests fail on HEAD: a stale pin of lovejoinBoxValue's answer
findings.scenario: Any PR from this branch runs web-wallet.yml's wasm job (`node --test "seedelf-web-wallet/wasm/tests/*.test.mjs"`, web-wallet.yml:159). gap-g8#6 added `minimum` to BoxValueResult, so the test 'a box of one token has a value…' fails. The lead's own run shows it: checks/ext-wasm-node.log, 'pass 59, fail 1', actual `{ least: '3620000', minimum: '1504190', suggested: '4000000', most: '9000000' }`.
findings.evidence: lovejoin-pools.test.mjs:176 `assert.deepEqual(of("1"), { least: "3620000", suggested: "4000000", most: "9000000" });`. G4a2's round1 lists only the Rust and Vitest pins it changed. The .mjs tests need the built module, which the fixers weren't allowed to build.
findings.fix: Expect `minimum: "1504190"` as well, and assert that minimum ≤ least, which is what the launch now refuses under.

verdicts.evidence:
This was a real bug at bd45ee21, but it is not on HEAD. HEAD is now 69d001e8, two commits past the 0.7.1 bump the task text names.

1. Where it came from. The lead ran the checks at bd45ee21 (calls/checks/ext-summary.txt: "start ... bd45ee21", "wasm-node exit 1 ℹ pass 59 ℹ fail 1"). The package was built at 17:16:22 and the node log was written at 17:16:25. At that commit, lovejoin-pools.test.mjs:176 still had the old pin: `assert.deepEqual(of("1"), { least: "3620000", suggested: "4000000", most: "9000000" });`. Meanwhile wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:3029-3044 (BoxValueResult) had gained `pub minimum: String`, and box_value at :3063-3076 fills it with `lovejoin::box_minimum(&probe, &params, token.as_ref())?`. The DECISIONS.md entry for gap-g8#6 lists the tests to update as lovejoin-flows.test.ts:922, flows.md:530, wasm/README.md:84 and wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:3009. It never names the .mjs test, so the fixers missed it.

2. The fix on HEAD. Commit 69d001e8 ("test: two tests the round's calls changed, now pinning what was decided", 17:49:11) changed that line. The pin is now at lovejoin-pools.test.mjs:177: `assert.deepEqual(of("1"), { least: "3620000", minimum: "1504190", suggested: "4000000", most: "9000000" });`, with a comment at :176 citing gap-g8#6. `git diff --stat bd45ee21..HEAD` touches only two docs/i18n JSONs, ja.json, e2e/extension.spec.ts and this test, so no Rust changed after the lead's build.

3. Run on HEAD the way CI runs it (web-wallet.yml:148-159 runs build.sh, then `node --test "seedelf-web-wallet/wasm/tests/*.test.mjs"` from seedelf-platform). I rsynced a copy, removed its pkg/, and ran wasm/build.sh fresh with toolchain 1.98.1, wasm-bindgen 0.2.128 and its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR. The new seedelf_wasm_bg.wasm is byte-identical to the tree's (sha256 3161dd59…a0a8). The node suite gives "ℹ tests 60, ℹ pass 60, ℹ fail 0", including "✔ a box of one token has a value ...". CI's wasm step is green on HEAD.

4. Other pins of the same answer still hold:
- The Rust test a_launchs_box_value_is_its_way_backs (wasm/tests/lovejoin_flows_test.rs:978-982) pins the ADA minimum at 1336100 and requires the token minimum to fall in 1_336_101..3_830_000, below least.
- a_box_of_one_token_has_a_box_value_and_none_is_refused checks its fields one by one, and the lead's cargo test passed 1013 / failed 0.
- The worker reads `minimum?: string` (extension/src/background/lovejoin-launch.ts:96) and refuses only when `box < BigInt(value.minimum)` (:254-256), as DECISIONS.md's OWNER line for gap-g8#6 asks.
- wasm/README.md:84 lists `{ least, minimum, suggested, most }`.
- The two Vitest failures at bd45ee21 were the i18n unchecked-draft gates (es/ja), not this field, and 75956e22 is the back-translation commit.
verdicts.fix_notes: Nothing to do on HEAD: 69d001e8 already pins `minimum: "1504190"` at lovejoin-pools.test.mjs:177, and the full node suite passes against a fresh build of HEAD. The finding's optional extra check, minimum ≤ least, would add nothing to this test. The exact pin already has 1504190 < 3620000, and the Rust test at lovejoin_flows_test.rs:981-982 checks the ordering for a token box. For the next round's process: a fixer who changes a WebAssembly result's shape should grep wasm/tests/*.test.mjs for the binding's JS name (here lovejoinBoxValue) beside the Rust and Vitest pins. Those tests run only against a built package, so the lead's post-merge node run is what catches them, as it did here.
verdicts.test:

findings.title: r2a#3, partly built: an amount's payment in parts still fills a part of ADA alone with a stranger's pile
findings.scenario: A private Make public of an amount large enough for parts. A last-part try comes back too large (too_much: tokens or computation), so in_parts builds another part through fit_part (lib.rs:4339). With fewer than 20 UTxOs that add something left, Room::picks takes 20 by Worth, the pile with its negative worth among them, and `most` spends every pick. The pile's tokens then go back as change on the user's ADA, though the amount didn't need them. privacy.md:174 now says every spend takes such a UTxO 'only for a token in it you're sending, when nothing else pays, or with Max'.
findings.who: stranger (sends the pile); a rare path
findings.evidence: lib.rs:4101-4106: `let at_most = if more { (group.len() + self.ada).min(self.k) } else { self.k }; … max_inputs_by(&from, …, at_most, |u| worth.of_utxo(u))`. Worth only ranks the pile last (i8 standing -1); it doesn't leave it out. G1a named it in round1 (siblings (2): 'a pile is last, but enters a part when fewer than 20 better UTxOs are left for it'). It isn't built or documented.
findings.fix: In Room::picks for an amount's parts (not Max's Fill::All), stop at the first pick whose worth is below zero, unless it holds a share token. Or say this edge in privacy.md:174.

verdicts.evidence:
Refuted on HEAD 69d001e8. The first half is true. Room::picks (wasm/src/lib.rs:4101-4106) fills a part of ADA alone with k UTxOs by worth through core max_inputs_by (seedelf-core/src/build.rs:3063-3064 sorts by Reverse(worth) and truncates). Worth only ranks a pile last (lib.rs:3893, standing -1), so when fewer than k UTxOs of worth >= 0 are left, the pile is picked. But nothing keeps that pick when the amount doesn't need it:

(1) When the part pays everything owed and no tokens come after it (lib.rs:4343), in_parts rebuilds it as `amount(picks, owed)` (:4344-4352). That is core's select_script_inputs, which takes the pile after everything else, then measured_or_more, which measures without it first (:3347). When it pays more than owed - keep but less than owed, it's rebuilt as `amount(picks, owed - keep)` (:4358), the same selection.

(2) The `most` result that spends every pick is kept only when it pays less than owed - keep (:4355-4356). Since the pile comes last, every UTxO of worth >= 0 in the part's pool is already in that part. For an amount of ADA that pool is all of `rest`: fit_part's `free` (:4234) holds everything when no tokens are owed. So only piles are left. The next last-part try is short, the loop breaks (:4389-4396), and the chain fallback tries anchors from the last back (:4407-4428). At the anchor before the pile's part, chained's ADA-alone Lean part (:4481) tries `amount(picks, owed)` first (:4485), which is core's selection again with the pile last. `parts.truncate(anchor)` (:4421) then drops the part that spent the pile. If the others can't pay, the payment is refused; that's the 'nothing else pays' case.

(3) The too-large trigger can't keep a pile either. `most` over the picks carries at least the tokens of the prefix core found too large. Room::after (:4124) then shrinks k, which drops the lowest worth, the pile, first. A short part of ADA alone does the same through room.fewer() (:4263).

So the trigger as described (a last-part try that's too much with fewer than 20 UTxOs of worth >= 0 left) needs core's search to grow through 4 or more piles to 23 inputs. SPEND_BUDGET_GUESS is 450M steps against a MAX_TX_BUDGET of 10B (build.rs:1180-1191), and the blind path returns at the first error that isn't short (build.rs:2694). That only happens for an amount the other UTxOs pay by the measured budget but not by the guessed one.

Test run, in a scratch copy with counters at those three places (copy and target deleted afterwards): 19 UTxOs of ADA alone, each 10 ₳ over its least, plus 5 strangers' piles of 200 tokens at their one-output least. Max is 216,810,378. An amount pays at most 215,340,799 measured and 215,160,778 by the guess. I took 7 amounts in that window: its low end, middle and high end with the pile in the first part's room, and the middle and high end with it in a later part's room (39 UTxOs, first part 20), both with no history and with the 39 split across two accounts. Results:
- One transaction was too much every time.
- Room::picks took a pile 9 times per plan.
- in_parts briefly kept a `most` part that spent a pile ("part 2 kept as `most` (paid 202274820 of 215250788 owed) spends 1 pile(s)").
- The later anchor went short, and the anchor before the pile's part built the last part from the 19 alone.
- Final plans were [19] or [20, 19] inputs, sent == amount, and 0 piles spent, for 7 of 7 amounts.

privacy.md:174's claim ("only for a token in it you're sending, when nothing else pays, or with Max") holds for parts of ADA alone. Not covered, and not this finding's scenario: parts that send tokens. There, Room::for_ada (lib.rs:4145) keeps `ada` when it cuts `h`, so a token part that's short of ADA even with every free UTxO could keep a pile's slot after its holders are cut.
verdicts.fix_notes:
No change needed for this finding. Don't apply the finder's fix (Room::picks stopping at the first UTxO of negative worth in an amount's parts). It would turn r2a#3's "last, never left out" (DECISIONS, owner-confirmed) into an exclusion inside parts. `adds` prices each pile alone, but change packs 20 tokens to an output, so several small piles can add something together. A part that then can't pick them would go short or hit NothingToPick, refusing an amount the ledger would take ("No paternalistic guards"). privacy.md:174 is accurate for parts of ADA alone, so the docs need no change either.

Optional: pin the behaviour with a test in wasm/tests/adds_less_than_nothing_test.rs. Use 19 UTxOs of ADA alone and 5 piles. Find the guess and measured maxima by binary search on build_withdraw, with the piles and without them. Make public an amount between the two, and also 20 UTxOs' Max plus it over 39 UTxOs. Assert `sent == amount` and that no part's inputs hold a pile. This needs no instrumentation. Optional doc line on Room::picks: a pile may be picked, but a part keeps it only when nothing else in the pool pays, since in_parts and chained rebuild a paying part through `amount`.

Unverified, separate from this finding: the anchor search's `Err(_) => break` (lib.rs:4426) ends at the first error that isn't short. Together with core's blind path returning the first such error (build.rs:2694), a pile big enough to be too large on its own might turn an amount in that guess/measured window into a "too large" refusal rather than an overpayment. If the lead wants it chased, it's its own finding.

findings.title: gap-g8#3's purpose (a sent note reads back whole in Activity) isn't met
findings.scenario: The user sends from the public account with a 300-character Japanese note, about 900 bytes. Core splits it into about 15 lines of 64 bytes, cut between characters since there's no space. Public Activity reads it back from chain with 14 added spaces. A 300-emoji note (300 code points, which the form and core take) is 600 UTF-16 units, so Activity cuts it to 250 emoji and an ellipsis.
findings.evidence: activity.ts:844 `const NOTE_MAX = 500;` and :854-856 `noteLines.join(" ")` … `text.length > NOTE_MAX ? text.slice(0, NOTE_MAX)+"…"` count UTF-16 units. note.rs:27 MAX_NOTE_CHARS = 500 counts chars, and split() (:112) cuts between characters where no space fits. CardanoSend.tsx counts `[...note]`. DECISIONS: 'Raise both caps together to 500, what Activity keeps of a note, so a note the wallet writes reads back whole in its own Activity'. G1b named it as a sibling in G6a's file; nobody took it.
findings.fix: In noteOf, cut by code points (`Array.from(text)`), and keep enough for the joined lines (500 plus a space a line). Or reword the claim in note.rs:19-24 and CardanoSend.tsx:52-56.

verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD 69d001e8 and confirmed by running the real WebAssembly. The pkg was built at 17:16 at bd45ee21, the last commit before HEAD that touches Rust.

Where the length is counted, and how:
- **Activity:** activity.ts:843-857 `noteOf` is unchanged this round. `git diff 984ff48f..HEAD` has no hunk in it; it was :693-705 before. It does `const text = noteLines.join(" ").trim(); ... return text.length > NOTE_MAX ? `${text.slice(0, NOTE_MAX)}…` : text;`, so it measures UTF-16 units of the lines joined with one space each.
- **Core:** note.rs:27 `MAX_NOTE_CHARS = 500` is checked as `text.chars().count()` (:52-53). `split` (:112-128) cuts at the last space inside 64 bytes and drops that space; with no space, it cuts between characters and adds nothing.
- **Form:** CardanoSend.tsx:57 `NOTE_MAX = 500` counts code points with `[...e.target.value]` (:396-399).

No other path guards it:
- A public entry's note comes only from `noteOf(tx.metadata)` (activity.ts:1045, :1076). `named` carries no note, and `pendingEntries` (incoming.ts:334) has none.
- `EntryNote` (Activity.tsx:407-418) shows it through `shownSiteText`. Its HIDDEN escapes Cf/Cc/Zl/Zp, not Cs, so a lone surrogate gets through.
- `.activity__note` has no line clamp. The CSV writes the same `e.note` (ui/activity.ts:231).
- The data layer's `tx_info` returns db-sync's JSON by label (seedelf-data api/src/public/tx.rs:193), the same shape as Koios.

Run results (note → what Activity shows):
- **480 Japanese characters:** 23 lines, 22 spaces added, 502 units. Cut, and the last 2 characters are lost.
- **500-character link with no spaces:** 8 lines, 7 spaces added. Cut, and the last 7 characters are lost. A 493-character one reads back; 494 is cut.
- **500 × 🌱, core's own "most" note (long_note_test.rs:162):** 32 lines. Activity keeps 242 whole emoji, then a lone \uD83C, then "…".
- **Ordinary 499-character note with spaces, ending in 🎉:** cut inside the emoji, ending "fo�…".
- **Control, 500 ASCII characters cut at spaces:** reads back exactly.

Corrections to the finding:
- The 300-character Japanese note is not cut: 15 lines, 14 spaces added, 314 units. The added spaces are the join documented at note.rs:67-69. They already happened at the old 64 cap (at most 3), so only the truncation is new.
- The 300-emoji note keeps 242 whole emoji plus a broken one, not 250.

G1b named this as a sibling in round1.json ("activity.ts:705 noteOf (G6a's file) keeps 500 UTF-16 units…"), and the shared notes list it too. Nobody changed `noteOf`.

**Who and how bad:** only the user, with their own note. Their Activity and the CSV show the note cut with "…", sometimes with a broken last character. The chain and explorers hold it whole. That's an edge case, so low.

The words "what Activity keeps of a note" are wider than the code in note.rs:22-26, CardanoSend.tsx:52-56, long_note_test.rs:9-10, payment-limits.test.ts:7-9, flows.md's note bullet and architecture.md's `Note::new` line.

What holds:
- Both caps were raised to 500 together, as decided, and core and the form both count code points.
- send.test.ts pins the refusal at 501.
- The transaction carries every character.
- No strings changed.

findings.title: e8b#1's residue: the forms count the fallback collateral as free, while the wallet's builds keep it
findings.scenario: A 1.9.1 user pressed Set on a stranger's 5 ₳ carrying a reference script (X), and also holds a plain 5 ₳ (Y). Home's and the forms' lock figure comes from listed()/locked(), which takes collateralOf(choices, fresh) without `own`, so it counts only X as kept and Y as free. readAccount (own=true) keeps X out as the choice and Y out as the collateral. So Max from the public account sends 5 ₳ less than the form's figure; the review shows the real amount.
findings.who: user (a choice saved by 1.9.1 or earlier)
findings.evidence: coin-control.ts:348 `const collateral = collateralOf(choices, fresh)?.utxo;` (no own). coin-control.ts:279-282 `const collateral = collateralOf(choices, utxos, own)…; const chosen = own ? collateralOf(choices, utxos)?.utxo : collateral; … p !== collateral && p !== chosen`. account.ts:199 passes `true`. G4b noted this in round1's left, unresolved.
findings.fix: Report the same collateral in the lock figure as the builds put up (Y in the residue), or count both X and Y as kept there.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD (69d001e8). I traced it end to end and a test shows it.

How the state arises. 1.9.1's Collateral page offered any pure 5 ₳ as its candidate (web-wallet/1.9.1 coin-control.ts:377, `isCollateralShaped` with no script or datum check). So a stranger's 5 ₳ carrying a reference script or a datum (X) could be saved as `choices.collateral`. On HEAD, use() (coin-control.ts:445-460) still takes any isCollateralShaped row, but its only caller, Collateral.tsx:165, now sends the collateralFits candidate. A choice that doesn't fit therefore comes only from 1.9.1 or earlier. The account also holds its own plain 5 ₳ (Y).

What the builds keep out:
- account.ts:199 calls `deps.coins.account(network, utxos, account, true)`.
- coin-control.ts:279 → :225 `chosen && (!own || collateralFits(chosen.utxo))` turns X down. :227-229 then return the oldest row that fits, which is Y.
- :280 `const chosen = own ? collateralOf(choices, utxos)?.utxo : collateral` is X.
- :282 filters out both X and Y.
- send.ts:123-124 (pay) reads readAccount, and Max spends all of those `utxos`.

What the figures count:
- balances.ts:321-323 withLocked → coins.locked → coin-control.ts:294 lists(…, false) → listed() → :348 `const collateral = collateralOf(choices, fresh)?.utxo;` (no own), which gives X.
- :370-371 mark only X as locked and collateral. :296 sums the locked rows, so Home's "{{amount}} ₳ locked" (Home.tsx:1139) says 5 ₳.
- Home.tsx:516-521 sets `free.cardano = withRewards(unlocked(balances.cardano), rewards)`; format.ts:455-462 takes the locked figure off the balance.

findings.title: seedelf-core's API change goes out as 0.7.1, and an older CLI built against it pays a script's address with no warning
findings.scenario: Once 0.7.1 is on crates.io, someone runs `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` without --locked. Cargo resolves seedelf-core ^0.7.0 to 0.7.1. CLI 0.7.0's sweep and remove gate on build::is_payable_address, which now passes a script's address, and that CLI has no warn_if_a_script. It then pays, say, the Seedelf contract's own address with no datum and no warning, where anyone can take it. Launch and AccountLaunch, all-public structs, also gain a public field, which breaks a struct literal downstream.
findings.evidence: bd45ee21: `seedelf-core = "0.7.1"`, `[workspace.package] version = "0.7.1"`. build.rs:3432-3434 is_payable_address is widened. launch.rs:122 and :465 add `pub cant_come_back`. CLAUDE.md: 'on 0.x Cargo reads a minor bump as breaking, which is the right regime for it'.
findings.fix: 0.8.0 for the workspace, or keep 0.7.1 knowingly and yank nothing.
findings.owner_question: The decision said 'a CLI patch release'. Is 0.7.1 still right for a core API whose payee check widened, or should it be 0.8.0?

verdicts.evidence:
The version problem is real, and it goes deeper than the finder said. The harm in the title is false: CLI 0.7.0 cannot be built against the 0.7.1 crates, so it never pays a script's address without a warning. Corrected title: "seedelf-core's breaking API changes go out as 0.7.1, so `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` without --locked stops compiling, and any crate on seedelf-core "0.7" breaks on update."

The guard the finder missed:
- Commit 03cf290e ("fix(cli): only the contract's script address holds a CLI wallet's rows") sits on web-wallet/whole-review before this round and has never been published. It changed the second parameter of six public functions in seedelf_core::utxos from `seedelf_policy_id: &str` to `contract: &Contract`. They are utxos.rs:53 collect_all_wallet_utxos, :81 find_seedelf_datum, :116 find_seedelf_utxo, :147 collect_wallet_utxos, :563 find_all_seedelfs and :613 count_lovelace_and_utxos.
- The published seedelf-core-0.7.0.crate is built from cda19571, the 0.7.0 tag (its .cargo_vcs_info.json says so). It has the `&str` forms at utxos.rs:85 and :111.
- CLI 0.7.0 passes `&chain.config.contract.seedelf_policy_id` at sweep.rs:151 and remove.rs:57, and at seven other call sites.
- I built tag 0.7.0's CLI with its published-style requirement, `seedelf-core = "0.7.0"`, against HEAD's crates. Cargo chose seedelf-core, -crypto, -koios and -display v0.7.1 for that requirement, then failed with nine E0308 errors. sweep.rs:151 and remove.rs:57 are among them.
- So no CLI 0.7.0 binary that uses the widened build::is_payable_address (build.rs:3432-3434) can be built. The silent payment would need a third-party crate that calls is_payable_address or sweep but none of the six changed functions. I know of no such crate.

What holds:
- Under Cargo's 0.x rule, 0.7.1 must be compatible with 0.7.0, and it isn't. The six utxos signatures above, all unpublished, ride this bump.
- This round adds `pub cant_come_back` to Launch (launch.rs:109-123, field at :122). At 0.7.0 all six of its fields are public, so a struct literal or an exhaustive pattern breaks. E0027 confirmed this.
- The finder is wrong that AccountLaunch is all public. It has nine private fields (launch.rs:449-457), so its new field at :465 breaks nothing.
- is_payable_address's widening and MAX_NOTE_CHARS going from 64 to 500 change behaviour but still compile.
- RELEASE.md publishes all five crates with one shared version.

Who can cause it and what it costs:
- A user who pins 0.7.0 without --locked gets a failed build. A developer whose crate depends on seedelf-core 0.7 breaks on `cargo update`.
- The README says `cargo install seedelf-cli` with no pin, which installs 0.7.1 and builds. Published CLI crates ship a Cargo.lock (checked in the cached seedelf-cli-0.5.0.crate) and a caret requirement, so `--locked` still installs 0.7.0 with core 0.7.0.
- No funds are at risk, and no stranger or site is involved.

Against DECISIONS:
- The approved texts say "CLI patch release" (r2a#3 at :16, r4#8 at :61, the plan at :851). Note 2 of g1b (:719) says core "needs a version bump either way" and doesn't say how big.
- CLAUDE.md:98, edited by this same bump, says a minor bump is the right regime when core's API moves.
- So bd45ee21 does what the decision says, and that breaks Cargo's compatibility promise. This is a question for the owner, not a coding slip.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Owner's choice. Either answer needs the finder's owner_question restated, because the risk is a failed build, not money.

(a) Recommended: 0.8.0 for the whole workspace.
- Use RELEASE.md's own block with version="0.8.0". It updates aiken.toml, `[workspace.package]`, the four `[workspace.dependencies]` lines and, through `cargo update --workspace`, the six Cargo.lock members.
- Change CLAUDE.md:98 to "(0.8.0 today)" and RELEASE.md's two examples to 0.8.0.
- Reword the round's "CLI patch release" lines and bd45ee21's message as a minor release. On 0.x, that is what tells Cargo core's API broke.
- Nothing needs yanking.

(b) Keep 0.7.1 knowingly.
- Write down that `cargo install seedelf-cli --version 0.7.0` needs --locked once 0.7.1 is out.
- Leave 0.7.0 unyanked.
- Restoring compatibility would take far more: six `&str` wrappers in utxos.rs, plus replacing Launch's new field with a method such as `Launch::cant_come_back(&self, params)` that computes check_usable from `self.pool`. Adding even a private field to an all-public struct still breaks callers.
- (b) is only sensible if the owner wants the "patch" label more than Cargo's semantics.

Either way:
- Drop AccountLaunch from the finding. Its new field is not breaking.
- The release check before tagging could build tag 0.7.0's CLI against the new crates, as the test below does. That would catch this every time.

findings.title: short.ts's TooLarge pattern also catches core's reference-script limit, and gives it the wrong advice
findings.scenario: A public Send or Max spends account UTxOs whose reference scripts total over 200 KiB. Core says '…bytes of reference scripts, over the network's limit of 204800. Spend fewer UTxOs holding one at once'. tooMany() now rewrites that as worker.parts.tooLarge: 'Send fewer tokens, or pay fewer recipients, at once'. send.ts:156 now routes every non-shortfall error through tooMany.
findings.who: stranger (would need about 13 planted UTxOs with 16 KiB scripts, so unreachable in practice)
findings.evidence: short.ts:32 `const TOO_LARGE = /over the network's limit of \d+/;` also matches build.rs:73's message.
findings.fix: Match TooLarge's own words: /This transaction would be \d+ bytes|One output would hold \d+ bytes/.
